title.zh: 卷一 本紀第一: 世紀
title.raw: 卷一 本紀第一: 世紀 Volume 1 Annals 1: Ancenstral Records

sentences.zh: 金之先，出靺鞨氏。

translations.literal: Of the Jin forebears, they issued from the Mohe clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin traced their origins to the Mohe people.

sentences.zh: 靺鞨本號勿吉。

translations.literal: Mohe was originally styled Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: The Mohe had formerly been known as the Wuji.

sentences.zh: 勿吉，古肅慎地也。

translations.literal: Wuji was the land of ancient Sushen.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuji inhabited the territory of the ancient Sushen.

sentences.zh: 元魏時，勿吉有七部：曰粟末部、曰伯咄部、曰安車骨部、曰拂涅部、曰號室部、曰黑水部、曰白山部。

translations.literal: In the Northern Wei era, Wuji had seven divisions: namely the Sumo division, the Boduo division, the Anchegu division, the Funie division, the Haoshi division, the Heishui division, and the Baishan division.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Wei the Wuji were divided into seven tribes: Sumo, Boduo, Anchegu, Funie, Haoshi, Heishui, and Baishan.

sentences.zh: 隋稱靺鞨，而七部並同。

translations.literal: The Sui styled them Mohe, and the seven divisions remained collectively the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui called them Mohe, and the seven divisions were treated as one people.

sentences.zh: 唐初，有黑水靺鞨、粟末靺鞨，其五部無聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tang, there were the Heishui Mohe and the Sumo Mohe; of the five other divisions nothing is heard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tang only the Heishui and Sumo Mohe are recorded; the other five divisions vanish from the sources.

sentences.zh: 粟末靺鞨始附高麗，姓大氏。

translations.literal: The Sumo Mohe at first attached themselves to Goryeo and bore the surname Da.
translations.idiomatic: The Sumo Mohe first submitted to Goryeo and took the clan name Da.

sentences.zh: 李績破高麗，粟末靺鞨保東牟山。

translations.literal: When Li Ji crushed Goryeo, the Sumo Mohe held Dongmou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Ji’s conquest of Goryeo, the Sumo Mohe withdrew to hold Dongmou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 後爲渤海，稱王，傳十餘世。

translations.literal: Later they became Parhae, styled themselves kings, and passed down the throne for more than ten generations.
translations.idiomatic: They later founded Parhae, took royal titles, and ruled for more than ten generations.

sentences.zh: 有文字、禮樂、官府、制度。

translations.literal: They had writing, ritual and music, government offices, and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: They possessed a script, court ritual and music, offices, and a full administrative order.

sentences.zh: 有五京、十五府、六十二州。

translations.literal: They had five capitals, fifteen fu, and sixty-two zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Their realm comprised five capitals, fifteen prefectures, and sixty-two districts.

sentences.zh: 黑水靺鞨居肅慎地，東瀕海，南接高麗，亦附於高麗。

translations.literal: The Heishui Mohe dwelt in Sushen territory, bordering the sea on the east and adjoining Goryeo on the south; they too were attached to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: The Heishui Mohe lived in the old Sushen lands, with the sea to the east and Goryeo to the south, and they likewise owed allegiance to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 嘗以兵十五萬衆助高麗拒唐太宗，敗于安市。

translations.literal: They once led an army of a hundred and fifty thousand to help Goryeo resist Emperor Taizong of Tang and were defeated at Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: They once fielded a hundred and fifty thousand men to aid Goryeo against Tang Taizong and were routed at Anshi.

sentences.zh: 開元中，來朝，置黑水府，以部長爲都督、刺史，置長史監之。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era they came to court; the Heishui prefecture was established, with the tribal chief made Protector-General and Prefect, and a Chief Secretary installed to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign they presented tribute; the court set up the Heishui prefecture, appointed the tribal leader Protector-General and prefect, and posted a chief secretary to supervise him.

sentences.zh: 賜都督姓李氏，名獻誠，領黑水經略使。

translations.literal: The Protector-General was granted the surname Li and the personal name Xiancheng, and was made Commissioner for Heishui Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Protector-General received the Tang surname Li and the name Xiancheng, and was named Commissioner for Heishui Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 其後渤海盛強，黑水役屬之，朝貢遂絕。

translations.literal: Thereafter Parhae grew powerful; the Heishui were subjected and made subordinate to them, and tribute ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Parhae rose in strength, the Heishui were reduced to vassalage and their tribute to the Tang ended.

sentences.zh: 五代時，契丹盡取渤海地，而黑水靺鞨附屬於契丹。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties period the Khitan seized all Parhae territory, and the Heishui Mohe came under Khitan rule.
translations.idiomatic: In the Five Dynasties the Khitan annexed Parhae’s lands, and the Heishui Mohe fell under Khitan authority.

sentences.zh: 其在南者籍契丹，號熟女直；

translations.literal: Those in the south were registered with the Khitan and were called the “settled Jurchen”;
translations.idiomatic: The southern groups were entered on Khitan registers and called the “civilized Jurchen”;

sentences.zh: 其在北者不在契丹籍，號生女直。

translations.literal: those in the north were not on the Khitan registry and were called the “wild Jurchen.”
translations.idiomatic: those in the north lay outside Khitan registration and were called the “wild Jurchen.”

sentences.zh: 生女直地有混同江、長白山，混同江亦號黑龍江，所謂「白山黑水」是也。

translations.literal: Wild Jurchen lands had the Huntong River and Changbai Mountain; the Huntong River was also called the Black Dragon River—what is meant by “White Mountain and Black Water.”
translations.idiomatic: The wild Jurchen homeland held the Huntong and Changbai Mountains; the Huntong was also known as the Black Dragon River—the “white mountain and black water” of their lore.

sentences.zh: 金之始祖諱函普，初從高麗來，年已六十餘矣。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor of the Jin, taboo name Huanpu, at first came from Goryeo when he was already more than sixty years old.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founding ancestor, whose name was tabooed as Huanpu, first arrived from Goryeo already past sixty.

sentences.zh: 兄阿古乃好佛，留高麗不肯從，曰：「後世子孫必有能相聚者，吾不能去也。

translations.literal: His elder brother Aguna was devoted to Buddhism, remained in Goryeo and would not follow him, saying: “In later generations descendants will surely be able to gather together again—I cannot leave.”
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Aguna, a devout Buddhist, stayed in Goryeo and refused to go, saying, “Our descendants will surely meet again one day—I cannot leave.”

sentences.zh: 」獨與弟保活里俱。

translations.literal: He alone went together with his younger brother Baohuoli.
translations.idiomatic: He set out with only his younger brother Baohuoli.

sentences.zh: 始祖居完顏部僕幹水之涯，保活里居耶懶。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor dwelt on the banks of the Pugan River in the Wanyan tribe; Baohuoli dwelt at Yelan.
translations.idiomatic: The founding ancestor settled on the Pugan River in Wanyan territory; Baohuoli made his home at Yelan.

sentences.zh: 其後胡十門以曷蘇館歸太祖，自言其祖兄弟三人相別而去，蓋自謂阿古乃之後。

translations.literal: Later Hutumen submitted the Hesuguan to Taizu and said of himself that his grandfather and three brothers had parted and gone separate ways—he claimed to be a descendant of Aguna.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hutumen brought the Hesuguan into Taizu’s service and declared that his grandfather and two brothers had split apart long ago—he held himself to be Aguna’s descendant.

sentences.zh: 石土門、迪古乃，保活里之裔也。

translations.literal: Shitumen and Digunai were descendants of Baohuoli.
translations.idiomatic: Shitumen and Digunai were of Baohuoli’s line.

sentences.zh: 及太祖敗遼兵於境上，獲耶律謝十，乃使梁福、斡荅刺招諭渤海人曰：「女直、渤海本同一家。

translations.literal: When Taizu defeated Liao troops on the frontier and captured Yelü Xieyu, he sent Liang Fu and Wodaci to summon and instruct the Parhae people, saying: “Jurchen and Parhae are originally of one family.”
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu routed the Liao on the border and took Yelü Xieyu prisoner, he sent Liang Fu and Wodaci to win over the Parhae, saying, “Jurchen and Parhae spring from one house.”

sentences.zh: 」蓋其初皆勿吉之七部也。

translations.literal: For at first they all belonged among the seven divisions of Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning they had all been among Wuji’s seven divisions.

sentences.zh: 始祖至完顏部，居久之，其部人嘗殺它族之人，由是兩族交惡，哄鬥不能解。

translations.literal: When the founding ancestor came to the Wanyan tribe and dwelt there a long time, men of the tribe once killed a man of another clan; hence the two clans became mutually hostile and quarreled in tumult, unable to reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: The founding ancestor had long lived among the Wanyan when tribesmen killed a man of another clan; the two sides turned on each other in a feud that would not end.

sentences.zh: 完顏部人謂始祖曰：「若能爲部人解此怨，使兩族不相殺，部有賢女，年六十而未嫁，當以相配，仍爲同部。

translations.literal: Men of the Wanyan tribe said to the founding ancestor: “If you can resolve this grievance for the tribesmen and make the two clans cease killing one another, there is a worthy woman in the tribe, sixty years old and still unmarried—we will give her to you in marriage and you shall remain of the same tribe.”
translations.idiomatic: The Wanyan told the founding ancestor, “Settle this blood-feud so the clans stop killing each other, and we will give you a worthy woman of the tribe—sixty and still unwed—to marry, and you shall count as one of us.”

sentences.zh: 」始祖曰：「諾。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor said: “I agree.”
translations.idiomatic: The founding ancestor said, “Very well.”

sentences.zh: 」乃自往諭之曰：「殺一人而鬥不解，損傷益多。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went in person to instruct them, saying: “If one man is killed and the fighting does not stop, wounds and losses only increase.”
translations.idiomatic: He went himself to reason with them: “One death has already set you at each other’s throats; if you go on, the wounded will only multiply.”

sentences.zh: 曷若止誅首亂者一人，部內以物納償汝，可以無鬥，而且獲利焉。

translations.literal: Why not simply execute the one who first stirred up the disorder, and have the tribe compensate you with goods? Then there need be no fighting—and you gain profit besides.
translations.idiomatic: “Execute the ringleader alone and let the tribe pay you in goods—you avoid further bloodshed and profit by it.”

sentences.zh: 」怨家從之。

translations.literal: The feuding party accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The aggrieved clan agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃爲約曰：「凡有殺傷人者，征其家人口一、馬十偶、牸牛十、黃金六兩，與所殺傷之家，即兩解，不得私鬥。

translations.literal: He thereupon made a covenant, saying: “Whenever anyone kills or wounds another, let there be levied from his household one person, ten pairs of horses, ten cows, and six liang of gold, given to the household of the injured party; then both sides shall be reconciled, and private fighting is forbidden.”
translations.idiomatic: He drew up a pact: “Whoever kills or injures another shall pay the victim’s kin one household member, ten pairs of horses, ten cattle, and six liang of gold; the matter is then closed, and private vendetta is forbidden.”

sentences.zh: 」曰：「謹如約。

translations.literal: They said: “We will strictly observe the covenant.”
translations.idiomatic: They answered, “We will abide by the pact.”

sentences.zh: 」女直之俗，殺人償馬牛三十，自此始。

translations.literal: Among Jurchen custom, the compensation of thirty horses and oxen for a killing began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: From this settlement dates the Jurchen rule that a life is paid for with thirty horses and cattle.

sentences.zh: 既備償如約，部衆信服之，謝以青牛一，並許歸六十之婦。

translations.literal: When compensation had been furnished as agreed, the tribesmen trusted him; they thanked him with one black ox and also promised him the sixty-year-old woman in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Once the payment was made as agreed, the tribe trusted him; they gave him a black ox in gratitude and betrothed him the sixty-year-old woman.

sentences.zh: 始祖乃以青牛爲聘禮而納之，並得其貲產。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor thereupon took the black ox as betrothal gift and married her, and also received her property.
translations.idiomatic: He took the black ox as bride-price, married her, and with her came her estate.

sentences.zh: 後生二男，長曰烏魯，次曰斡魯，一女曰注思板，遂爲完顏部人。

translations.literal: Later she bore two sons—the elder called Wulu, the younger Wolu—and one daughter called Zhushiban; he thus became a man of the Wanyan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: She later bore two sons, Wulu and Wolu, and a daughter, Zhushiban; he was thereby enrolled among the Wanyan.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年，追諡景元皇帝，廟號始祖。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously enfeoffed as Emperor Jingyuan, with temple name Founding Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year fourteen he was posthumously titled Emperor Jingyuan, with the temple name Founding Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏曰光陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year four his tomb was named Guangling.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡始祖懿憲景元皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his posthumous title was increased to Founding Ancestor Emperor Yixian Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was raised to Founding Ancestor Emperor Yixian Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 子德帝，諱烏魯。

translations.literal: His son, Emperor De, taboo name Wulu.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Emperor De, whose name was tabooed as Wulu.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年，追諡德皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously enfeoffed as Emperor De.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year fourteen he was posthumously titled Emperor De.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏曰熙陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year four his tomb was named Xiling.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡淵穆玄德皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his posthumous title was increased to Emperor Yuanmu Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was raised to Emperor Yuanmu Xuande.

sentences.zh: 子安帝，諱跋海。

translations.literal: His son, Emperor An, taboo name Bahai.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Emperor An, whose name was tabooed as Bahai.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年，追諡安皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously enfeoffed as Emperor An.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year fourteen he was posthumously titled Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏建陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Jianling.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year four his tomb was named Jianling.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡和靖慶安皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, additional posthumous titles were conferred: Emperor Hejing Qingan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year additional posthumous titles were conferred: Emperor Hejing Qingan (Harmonious and Tranquil, Celebrating Peace).

sentences.zh: 子獻祖，諱綏可。

translations.literal: His son was Xianzu, taboo name Suikede.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xianzu (Founding Ancestor), whose taboo name was Suikede.

sentences.zh: 黑水舊俗無室廬，負山水坎地，梁木其上，覆以土，夏則出隨水草以居，冬則入處其中，遷徙不常。

translations.literal: The old custom of the Black Water [people] had no houses or lodges. Taking advantage of ravine land amid mountains and waters, they set beams atop it and covered them with earth. In summer they went out to live following the grasses and waters; in winter they dwelt within these structures. They moved constantly without fixed abode.
translations.idiomatic: The Black Water Jurchen once had no fixed houses. They chose ravine ground among mountains and streams, laid beams, and roofed them with earth. In summer they moved with pasture and water; in winter they lived inside these shelters, always shifting and never settled.

sentences.zh: 獻祖乃徙居海古水，耕墾樹藝，始築室，有棟宇之制，人呼其地爲納葛里。

translations.literal: Xianzu then moved to dwell on the Haigu River, ploughing, opening fields, planting trees and crops, and for the first time building houses with the structure of rafters and beams. People called the place Nageli.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu then moved to the Haigu River, opened fields, planted crops, and for the first time built framed houses with rafters and beams. The place was called Nageli.

sentences.zh: 納葛里者，漢語居室也。

translations.literal: Nageli means "dwelling" in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Nageli means "dwelling place" in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 自此遂定居于安出虎水之側矣。

translations.literal: From this time they settled permanently on the banks of the Anchuhu River.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they settled permanently on the banks of the Anchuhu River.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年，追諡定昭皇帝，廟號獻祖。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui, he was posthumously honoured as Emperor Dingzhao, with temple name Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously honoured as Emperor Dingzhao, with the temple name Xianzu (Founding Ancestor).

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏曰輝陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong, his burial mound was named Huiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Huiling (Splendid Mound).

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡獻祖純烈定昭皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, additional titles were conferred: Xianzu, Pure and Ardent Emperor Dingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year additional titles were conferred: Xianzu, Pure and Ardent Emperor Dingzhao.

sentences.zh: 子昭祖，諱石魯，剛毅質直。

translations.literal: His son was Zhaozu, taboo name Shilu, resolute, firm, and plain in character.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhaozu (Illustrious Ancestor), taboo name Shilu — resolute, steadfast, and plain in character.

sentences.zh: 生女直無書契，無約束，不可檢制。

translations.literal: The uncooked Jurchen had no written records or tally sticks, no regulations or restraints, and could not be controlled or measured.
translations.idiomatic: The uncooked Jurchen kept no writing or tallies, no laws or restraints; they could not be governed or checked.

sentences.zh: 昭祖欲稍立條教，諸父、部人皆不悅，欲坑殺之。

translations.literal: Zhaozu wished to establish regulations by degrees. The paternal uncles and tribesmen were all displeased and wanted to bury him alive to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu wished to introduce regulations little by little. His paternal uncles and tribesmen were displeased and plotted to bury him alive.

sentences.zh: 已被執，叔父謝里忽知部衆將殺昭祖，曰：「吾兄子，賢人也，必能承家，安輯部衆，此輩奈何輒欲坑殺之！

translations.literal: He had already been seized. His uncle Shelilie, learning that the tribesmen were about to kill Zhaozu, said: "My brother's son is a worthy man; he will surely be able to sustain the clan and pacify the tribe. How can these people so rashly wish to bury him alive!
translations.idiomatic: He had already been seized. His uncle Shelilie, learning that the tribe meant to kill Zhaozu, cried, "My brother's son is a worthy man who can sustain our house and settle the tribe. How can you people so rashly try to bury him alive!

sentences.zh: 」亟往，彎弓注矢射於衆中，劫執者皆散走，昭祖乃得免。

translations.literal: " He hurried there, drew his bow and nocked an arrow, and shot into the crowd. Those holding Zhaozu captive all scattered and fled, and Zhaozu thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: " He rushed over, drew his bow, nocked an arrow, and shot into the crowd. Those holding Zhaozu scattered and fled, and Zhaozu escaped.

sentences.zh: 昭祖稍以條教爲治，部落浸強。

translations.literal: Zhaozu gradually governed by regulations, and the tribe grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu gradually ruled by regulations, and the tribe grew steadily stronger.

sentences.zh: 遼以惕隱官之。

translations.literal: The Liao appointed him as tiyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao appointed him tiyi (imperial son-in-law commissioner).

sentences.zh: 諸部猶以舊俗，不肯用條教。

translations.literal: The various tribes still followed the old customs and refused to adopt the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The other tribes still clung to the old ways and refused to accept the regulations.

sentences.zh: 昭祖耀武至於青嶺、白山，順者撫之，不從者討伐之，入于蘇濱、耶懶之地，所至克捷，還經僕燕水。

translations.literal: Zhaozu displayed martial prowess as far as the Green Mountains and White Mountains. Those who submitted he soothed; those who did not he chastised. He entered the lands of Subin and Yelan, triumphing wherever he went, and returned by way of the Puyan River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu showed force as far as the Green Mountains and White Mountains: he soothed those who submitted and attacked those who refused. He penetrated Subin and Yelan, winning wherever he went, and returned by the Puyan River.

sentences.zh: 僕燕，漢語惡瘡也。

translations.literal: Puyan means "malignant sore" in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Puyan means "malignant sore" in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 昭祖惡其地名，雖已困憊，不肯止。

translations.literal: Zhaozu hated the place name; though already exhausted, he would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu loathed the name of the place; though already spent, he would not halt.

sentences.zh: 行至姑里甸，得疾。

translations.literal: When he reached Guli Meadow, he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Guli Meadow he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 迨夜，寢於村舍。

translations.literal: Toward nightfall he lodged in a village dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: At nightfall he lodged in a village house.

sentences.zh: 有盜至，遂中夜啟行，至逼剌紀村止焉。

translations.literal: Thieves came, so he set out at midnight and halted at Bilaqi Village.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves appeared, so he set out again in the middle of the night and stopped at Bilaqi Village.

sentences.zh: 是夕，卒。

translations.literal: That very night he died.
translations.idiomatic: That same night he died.

sentences.zh: 載柩而行，遇賊于路，奪柩去。

translations.literal: Bearing the coffin onward, they met bandits on the road who seized the coffin and carried it off.
translations.idiomatic: As they carried the coffin along the road, bandits seized it and made off with it.

sentences.zh: 部衆追賊與戰，復得柩。

translations.literal: The tribesmen pursued the bandits and fought; they recovered the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen pursued the bandits, fought them, and recovered the coffin.

sentences.zh: 加古部人蒲虎復來襲之，垂及，蒲虎問諸路人曰：「石魯柩去此幾何？

translations.literal: Puhu of the Jagü tribe came to attack again. When they were almost upon them, Puhu asked passersby on the road: "How far from here is Shilu's coffin?
translations.idiomatic: Puhu of the Jagü tribe attacked again. As he was about to overtake them, Puhu asked travellers on the road, "How far from here is Shilu's coffin?

sentences.zh: 」其人曰：「遠矣，追之不及也。

translations.literal: " They replied: "It is far; you cannot overtake it.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "It is far off; you cannot catch up.

sentences.zh: 」蒲虎遂止。

translations.literal: " Puhu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Puhu then gave up the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 於是乃得歸葬焉。

translations.literal: Only then were they able to return and bury him.
translations.idiomatic: Only then could they return and bury him.

sentences.zh: 生女直之俗，至昭祖時稍用條教，民頗聽從，尚未有文字，無官府，不知歲月晦朔，是以年壽修短莫得而考焉。

translations.literal: Among the customs of the uncooked Jurchen, by the time of Zhaozu regulations were somewhat in use and the people largely obeyed; yet there were still no written characters, no government offices, and no knowledge of months, years, new moons, or the moon's last day — so the length and shortness of lives could not be determined.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhaozu's day the uncooked Jurchen had begun to follow regulations and the people largely obeyed, but they still had no writing, no offices, and no reckoning of months, years, or new and full moons — so no one could tell how long anyone had lived.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，追諡成襄皇帝，廟號昭祖。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui, he was posthumously honoured as Emperor Chengxiao, with temple name Zhaozu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously honoured as Emperor Chengxiao, with the temple name Zhaozu (Illustrious Ancestor).

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，藏號安陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong, the burial mound was named Anling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong the burial mound was named Anling (Peace Mound).

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡昭祖武惠成襄皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, additional titles were conferred: Zhaozu, Martial and Gracious Emperor Chengxiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year additional titles were conferred: Zhaozu, Martial and Gracious Emperor Chengxiao.

sentences.zh: 子景祖，諱烏古乃。

translations.literal: His son was Jingzu, taboo name Wugunai.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jingzu (Resplendent Ancestor), taboo name Wugunai.

sentences.zh: 遼太平元年辛酉歲生。

translations.literal: He was born in the xinyou year, the first year of the Liao Taiping era.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the xinyou year, the first year of the Liao Taiping reign.

sentences.zh: 自始祖至此，已六世矣。

translations.literal: From the founding ancestor to this point, there had already been six generations.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding ancestor to this point there had been six generations.

sentences.zh: 景祖稍役屬諸部，自白山、耶悔、統門、耶懶、土骨論之屬，以至五國之長，皆聽命。

translations.literal: Jingzu gradually brought the various tribes under his authority. From the White Mountains, Yehei, Tongmen, Yelan, Tugulun, and their kind, down to the chiefs of the Five States — all obeyed his commands.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu gradually brought the tribes under his command — from the White Mountains, Yehei, Tongmen, Yelan, and Tugulun, down to the chiefs of the Five States, all obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 是時，遼之邊民有逃而歸者。

translations.literal: At this time there were border people of the Liao who fled and came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Liao border people fled and came over to him.

sentences.zh: 及遼以兵徙鐵勒、烏惹之民，鐵勒、烏惹多不肯徙，亦逃而來歸。

translations.literal: When the Liao used troops to relocate the peoples of Tiele and Wunie, many of the Tiele and Wunie refused to move and also fled to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao moved the Tiele and Wunie peoples by force, many refused to relocate and fled to join him as well.

sentences.zh: 遼使曷魯林牙將兵來索逋逃之民。

translations.literal: The Liao sent Helu linya with troops to demand back the fugitive people.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao sent Commissioner Helu with troops to recover the fugitives.

sentences.zh: 景祖恐遼兵深入，盡得山川道路險易，或將圖之，乃以計止之曰：「兵若深入，諸部必驚擾，變生不測，逋戶亦不可得，非計也。

translations.literal: Jingzu feared that if Liao troops penetrated deeply they would learn all the mountains, rivers, roads, and passes in their strength and weakness, and might then plot against him. He therefore used a stratagem to stop them, saying: "If the army penetrates deeply, the tribes will surely be alarmed and disturbed; unforeseen changes may arise, and the fugitive households likewise cannot be obtained. It is not a sound plan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu feared that if Liao troops marched deep into his country they would learn every mountain, river, road, and pass — and might then turn against him. He therefore stopped them with a stratagem, saying, "If your army goes deep, the tribes will be alarmed and unforeseen trouble may arise; you will not recover the fugitives either. That is no good plan.

sentences.zh: 」曷魯以爲然，遂止其軍，與曷魯自行索之。

translations.literal: " Helu considered this reasonable, halted the army, and went in person with Jingzu to search for them.
translations.idiomatic: " Helu agreed, halted the army, and he and Jingzu went in person to search for the fugitives.

sentences.zh: 是時，鄰部雖稍從，孩懶水烏林答部石顯尚拒阻不服。

translations.literal: At this time, although neighbouring tribes had somewhat submitted, Shixian of the Wulin'a tribe on the Hailan River still resisted and would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: By then neighbouring tribes had largely submitted, but Shixian of the Wulin'a tribe on the Hailan River still resisted.

sentences.zh: 攻之，不克。

translations.literal: They attacked him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked him but could not defeat him.

sentences.zh: 景祖以計告於遼主，遼主遣使責讓石顯。

translations.literal: Jingzu informed the Liao sovereign of his stratagem; the Liao sovereign sent envoys to rebuke Shixian.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu laid his plan before the Liao sovereign, who sent envoys to rebuke Shixian.

sentences.zh: 石顯乃遣其子婆諸刊入朝，遼主厚賜遣還。

translations.literal: Shixian thereupon sent his son Pozhuokan to court; the Liao sovereign richly rewarded him and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian then sent his son Pozhuokan to court; the Liao sovereign richly rewarded him and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 其後石顯與婆諸刊入見遼主於春蒐。

translations.literal: Subsequently Shixian and Pozhuokan went to pay court to the Liao sovereign at the spring hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shixian and Pozhuokan attended the Liao sovereign at the spring hunt.

sentences.zh: 遼主乃留石顯於邊地，而遣婆諸刊還所部。

translations.literal: The Liao sovereign detained Shixian at the border region and sent Pozhuokan back to his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao sovereign kept Shixian at the frontier and sent Pozhuokan back to his tribe.

sentences.zh: 景祖之謀也。

translations.literal: This was Jingzu's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: This was Jingzu's stratagem.

sentences.zh: 既而五國蒲聶部節度使拔乙門叛遼，鷹路不通。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, Ba Yimen, military commissioner of the Punic branch of the Five States, rebelled against Liao, and the hawk-road was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ba Yimen, commissioner of the Five States’ Punic division, rebelled against Liao and cut the hawk-road tribute route.

sentences.zh: 遼人將討之，先遣同幹來諭旨。

translations.literal: The Liao were about to campaign against him; they first sent Tonggan to announce the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao prepared a punitive expedition and first sent Tonggan to deliver the sovereign’s orders.

sentences.zh: 景祖曰：「可以計取。

translations.literal: Jingzu said: “He can be taken by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu said, “Take him by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 若用兵，彼將走保險阻，非歲月可平也。

translations.literal: If troops are used, he will flee to hold the defiles and passes; he cannot be pacified in a matter of months.”
translations.idiomatic: Send an army and he will flee into the passes; you will not finish him in months.”

sentences.zh: 」遼人從之。

translations.literal: The Liao accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao agreed.

sentences.zh: 蓋景祖終畏遼兵之入其境也，故自以爲功。

translations.literal: For Jingzu had always feared Liao troops entering his territory; therefore he took credit for the stratagem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu had always dreaded a Liao march into his lands, and so he claimed the plan as his own success.

sentences.zh: 於是景祖陽與拔乙門爲好，而以妻子爲質，襲而擒之，獻於遼主。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jingzu feigned friendship with Ba Yimen, left his wife and children as hostages, then attacked and seized him, and presented him to the Liao sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned friendship with Ba Yimen, left wife and children as hostages, then struck and captured him and sent him to the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 遼主召見於寢殿，燕賜加等，以爲生女直部族節度使。

translations.literal: The Liao sovereign summoned him to the sleeping hall, feasted him with extraordinary rewards, and made him military commissioner of the Uncooked Jurchen tribal divisions.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao sovereign received him in the private hall, feasted him with exceptional gifts, and appointed him military commissioner of the uncooked Jurchen tribes.

sentences.zh: 遼人呼節度使爲太師，金人稱都太師者自此始。

translations.literal: The Liao called military commissioners “Grand Preceptor”; the Jin use of the title Chief Grand Preceptor began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao called commissioners “Grand Preceptor”; from this time the Jin title Chief Grand Preceptor dates.

sentences.zh: 遼主將刻印與之，景祖不肯系遼籍，辭曰：「請俟他日。

translations.literal: The Liao sovereign wished to engrave a seal and give it to him; Jingzu refused to be entered on the Liao registers, declining: “Please wait for another day.”
translations.idiomatic: The Liao sovereign meant to engrave a seal for him; Jingzu refused Liao registration, saying, “Let that wait for another day.”

sentences.zh: 」遼主終欲與之，遣使來。

translations.literal: The Liao sovereign still wished to give it; envoys were sent.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign still insisted and sent envoys.

sentences.zh: 景祖詭使部人揚言曰：「主公若受印系籍，部人必殺之！

translations.literal: Jingzu secretly had tribesmen spread word: “If our lord accepts the seal and registration, the tribesmen will surely kill him!”
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu secretly had his people proclaim, “If our lord takes the seal and enters the register, the tribe will kill him!”

sentences.zh: 」用是以拒之，遼使乃還。

translations.literal: With this he refused; the Liao envoys returned.
translations.idiomatic: On that pretext he refused, and the Liao envoys withdrew.

sentences.zh: 既爲節度使，有官屬，紀綱漸立矣。

translations.literal: Now that he was military commissioner, he had subordinate officials, and order was gradually established.
translations.idiomatic: As commissioner he had officers and retainers, and government by degrees took shape.

sentences.zh: 生女直舊無鐵，鄰國有以甲胄來鬻者，傾貲厚賈以與貿易，亦令昆弟族人皆售之。

translations.literal: The Uncooked Jurchen formerly had no iron; when neighboring states brought armor to sell, he spent his wealth at high prices to trade for it, and also had brothers and clansmen sell theirs.
translations.idiomatic: The uncooked Jurchen had no iron of their own; when neighbors offered armor for sale he paid lavishly to buy it and had kinsmen trade as well.

sentences.zh: 得鐵既多，因之以修弓矢，備器械，兵勢稍振，前後願附者衆。

translations.literal: Once iron was abundant, he thereby repaired bows and arrows and prepared weapons; military strength gradually revived, and many came to attach themselves before and after.
translations.idiomatic: With iron in hand he had bows and gear made ready; his forces strengthened, and clans came over in growing numbers.

sentences.zh: 斡泯水蒲察部、泰神忒保水完顏部、統門水溫蒂痕部、神隱水完顏部，皆相繼來附。

translations.literal: The Pucha division on the Wenmin River, the Wanyan division on the Taishen Tebao River, the Wentihen division on the Tongmen River, and the Wanyan division on the Shenyin River all came to attach themselves in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Pucha on the Wenmin, the Wanyan on the Taishen Tebao, the Wentihen on the Tongmen, and the Wanyan on the Shenyin rivers all submitted in turn.

sentences.zh: 景祖爲人寬恕，能容物，平生不見喜慍。

translations.literal: Jingzu was forgiving by nature, able to bear with others; in life he never showed joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu was magnanimous and forbearing; through his life he never showed pleasure or wrath.

sentences.zh: 推財與人，分食解衣，無所吝惜。

translations.literal: He gave away wealth to others, shared food and stripped off garments—nothing did he stint.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away goods, shared his food, and stripped off his own clothes for others—he spared nothing.

sentences.zh: 人或忤之，亦不念。

translations.literal: If someone offended him, he did not hold it in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Those who crossed him he did not bear grudges against.

sentences.zh: 先時，有叛去者，遣人諭誘之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when some had rebelled and left, he sent men to persuade and entice them back.
translations.idiomatic: When men had deserted him before, he sent envoys to coax them home.

sentences.zh: 叛者曰：「汝主，活羅也。

translations.literal: The rebels said: “Your lord is a Huoluo.”
translations.idiomatic: The deserters replied, “Your master is a huoluo.”

sentences.zh: 活羅，吾能獲之，吾豈能爲活羅屈哉！

translations.literal: “A Huoluo—I can catch one; how could I bow to a Huoluo!”
translations.idiomatic: “A huoluo—we can snare one anytime. Why should we bow to a huoluo?”

sentences.zh: 」活羅，漢語慈烏也。

translations.literal: Huoluo is the Chinese “compassionate crow.”
translations.idiomatic: Huoluo means “kindly crow” in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 北方有之，狀如大雞，善啄物，見馬牛橐駝脊間有瘡，啄其脊間食之，馬牛輒死，若饑不得食，雖砂石亦食之。

translations.literal: The north has it; shaped like a large fowl, good at pecking; when it sees sores on the backs of horses, cattle, and camels, it pecks and eats there—the beasts die; if hungry and finding no food, it eats even sand and stone.
translations.idiomatic: It lives in the north, large as a fowl and fierce at pecking. It spots sores on horses, cattle, and camels, pecks the wound, and the beast dies; starving, it will eat even grit and stone.

sentences.zh: 景祖嗜酒好色，飲啖過人，時人呼曰活羅，故彼以此訕之，亦不以介意。

translations.literal: Jingzu loved wine and women, eating and drinking beyond others; people of the time called him Huoluo; therefore they mocked him thus, yet he did not mind.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu drank and womanized beyond measure, and men nicknamed him Huoluo; they taunted him with the bird, and he took no offense.

sentences.zh: 其後訕者力屈來降，厚賜遣還。

translations.literal: Later the mockers, exhausted, came to surrender; he richly rewarded them and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: When the taunters were spent and came in, he gave them rich gifts and sent them away again.

sentences.zh: 曷懶水有率衆降者，錄其歲月姓名，即遣去，俾復其故。

translations.literal: On the Helan River some came leading masses to surrender; he recorded their years, months, and names, then sent them away, restoring them to their former status.
translations.idiomatic: On the Helan some arrived leading their bands; he noted their names and dates, then dismissed them to their old lives.

sentences.zh: 人以此益信服之。

translations.literal: People thereby trusted and obeyed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The people trusted him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 遼鹹雍八年，五國沒拈部謝野勃堇叛遼，鷹路不通。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Liao Xianyong, the bojin Xieye of the Mojie division of the Five States rebelled against Liao, and the hawk-road was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: In Liao Xianyong year eight, Xieye, bojin of the Five States’ Mojie division, rebelled and again blocked the hawk-road.

sentences.zh: 景祖伐之，謝野來禦。

translations.literal: Jingzu campaigned against him; Xieye came out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu marched against him; Xieye met him in the field.

sentences.zh: 景祖被重鎧，率衆力戰。

translations.literal: Jingzu donned heavy armor and led the masses in fierce battle.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu put on heavy mail and led his men in a hard fight.

sentences.zh: 謝野兵敗，走拔里邁濼。

translations.literal: Xieye's army was defeated; he fled to the Bali Mai marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye was beaten and fled toward the Bali Mai marsh.

sentences.zh: 時方十月，冰忽解，謝野不能軍，衆皆潰去，乃旋師。

translations.literal: It was just the tenth month; the ice suddenly broke up; Xieye could not keep his army; the masses all scattered; then he withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: It was only the tenth month when the ice broke early; Xieye could not hold his host, his men scattered, and Jingzu turned homeward.

sentences.zh: 道中遇逋亡，要遮險阻，晝夜拒戰，比至部已憊。

translations.literal: On the road he met fugitives who blocked the defiles; day and night they resisted in battle; by the time he reached his tribe he was already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives ambushed him in the passes and fought day and night; he reached his tribe worn out.

sentences.zh: 即往見遼邊將達魯骨，自陳敗謝野功。

translations.literal: He thereupon went to see the Liao border general Dalugu and declared his merit in defeating Xieye.
translations.idiomatic: He went at once to the Liao frontier commander Dalugu to report his victory over Xieye.

sentences.zh: 行次來流水，未見達魯骨，疾作而復，卒於家，年五十四。

translations.literal: Passing by the Laishui River, before he saw Dalugu, illness seized him and relapsed; he died at home, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: On the Laishui, before he could see Dalugu, his old illness returned; he died at home, aged fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年，追諡惠桓皇帝，廟號景祖。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui, posthumously titled Emperor Huihuan, temple name Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year fourteen he was posthumously titled Emperor Huihuan, with the temple name Jingzu (Resplendent Ancestor).

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，藏號定陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong, burial mound named Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year four his tomb was named Dingling.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡景祖英烈惠桓皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, additional title: Jingzu, Heroic and Illustrious Emperor Huihuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was raised to Jingzu, Heroic and Illustrious Emperor Huihuan.

sentences.zh: 第二子襲節度使，是爲世祖，諱劾里缽。

translations.literal: The second son succeeded as military commissioner; this was Shizu, taboo name Helibo.
translations.idiomatic: His second son inherited the commissionership—this was Shizu (World Ancestor), taboo name Helibo.

sentences.zh: 生女直之俗，生子年長即異居。

translations.literal: In the custom of the Uncooked Jurchen, when sons grew older they lived apart.
translations.idiomatic: Among the uncooked Jurchen, sons set up separate households once grown.

sentences.zh: 景祖九子，元配唐括氏生劾者，次世祖，次劾孫，次肅宗，次穆宗。

translations.literal: Jingzu had nine sons; the primary wife, of the Tangguo clan, bore Hezhe, next Shizu, next Hesun, next Suzong, next Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu had nine sons. His principal wife, of the Tangguo clan, bore Hezhe, then Shizu, Hesun, Suzong, and Muzong.

sentences.zh: 及當異居，景祖曰：「劾者柔和，可治家務。

translations.literal: When it came time to live apart, Jingzu said: “Hezhe is gentle and mild—he can manage household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When they were to divide households, Jingzu said, “Hezhe is mild and fit to keep the home.

sentences.zh: 劾里缽有器量智識，何事不成。

translations.literal: Helibo has capacity and wisdom; what could he not accomplish?
translations.idiomatic: Helibo has judgment and wit—what could he not achieve?

sentences.zh: 劾孫亦柔善人耳。

translations.literal: Hesun is also a gentle and good man.”
translations.idiomatic: Hesun too is a gentle, decent man.”

sentences.zh: 」乃命劾者與世祖同居，劾孫與肅宗同居。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Hezhe to live with Shizu, and Hesun with Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Hezhe to remain with Shizu and Hesun with Suzong.

sentences.zh: 景祖卒，世祖繼之。

translations.literal: When Jingzu died, Shizu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzu died, Shizu took his place.

sentences.zh: 世祖卒，肅宗繼之。

translations.literal: When Shizu died, Suzong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu died, Suzong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 肅宗卒，穆宗繼之。

translations.literal: When Suzong died, Muzong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong died, Muzong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗復傳世祖之子，至於太祖，竟登大位焉。

translations.literal: Muzong in turn transmitted [the line] to a son of Shizu; down to Taizu, [one] at last ascended the great throne.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong passed the line back to Shizu’s line, and in the end Taizu (Grand Ancestor) won the throne.

sentences.zh: 世祖，遼重熙八年己卯歲生。

translations.literal: Shizu was born in the ji-mao year, the eighth year of Liao Chongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu (World Ancestor) was born in the ji-mao year of Liao Chongxi (1039).

sentences.zh: 遼鹹雍十年，襲節度使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Liao Xianyong he succeeded to the military commissionership.
translations.idiomatic: In Liao Xianyong year ten (1074) he inherited the commissionership.

sentences.zh: 景祖異母弟跋黑有異志，世祖慮其爲變，加意事之，不使將兵，但爲部長。

translations.literal: Jingzu’s younger brother by a different mother, Bahai, harbored a different intent; Shizu feared he would rebel, treated him with special care, did not let him command troops, but only made him a sub-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu’s half-brother Bahai nursed other ambitions. Shizu feared a coup, courted him carefully, kept him from leading troops, and made him only a section chief.

sentences.zh: 跋黑遂誘桓赧、散達、烏春、窩謀罕爲亂，及間諸部使貳于世祖。

translations.literal: Bahai thereupon incited Huannan, Sanda, Wuchun, and Womouhan to rebellion, and set factions among the tribes to turn against Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Bahai then drew Huannan, Sanda, Wuchun, and Womouhan into revolt and sowed defection among the tribes against Shizu.

sentences.zh: 世祖猶欲撫慰之，語在跋黑、桓赧等傳中。

translations.literal: Shizu still wished to soothe them—the account is in the biographies of Bahai, Huannan, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu still tried conciliation; the story is told in the biographies of Bahai, Huannan, and the others.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗買加古部鍛工烏不屯被甲九十，烏春欲托此以爲兵端，世祖還其甲，語在《烏春傳》。

translations.literal: Shizu once bought ninety suits of armor from Wubutun, a smith of the Jiagu tribe; Wuchun wished to use this as a pretext for war; Shizu returned the armor—the account is in the “Biography of Wuchun.”
translations.idiomatic: Shizu once bought ninety corselets from Wubutun, a Jiagu smith. Wuchun tried to turn the purchase into a casus belli; Shizu sent the armor back—the full tale is in the Biography of Wuchun.

sentences.zh: 部中有流言曰：「欲生則附于跋黑，欲死則附於劾里缽、頗剌淑。

translations.literal: A saying circulated in the tribe: “If you wish to live, attach yourself to Bahai; if you wish to die, attach yourself to Helibo and Polasu.”
translations.idiomatic: A proverb ran through the tribe: “Want to live—follow Bahai; want to die—follow Helibo and Polasu.”

sentences.zh: 」世祖聞之，疑焉。

translations.literal: When Shizu heard it, he was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu heard it and grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 無以察之，乃佯爲具裝，欲有所往者，陰遣人揚言曰：「寇至！

translations.literal: Unable to investigate, he feigned preparing equipment as though about to go somewhere, and secretly had men spread word: “The enemy is coming!
translations.idiomatic: He could not test loyalties openly, so he pretended to arm for a march and secretly spread word: “The enemy is here!

sentences.zh: 」部衆聞者莫知虛實，有保于跋黑之室者，有保于世祖之室者，世祖乃盡得兄弟部屬向背彼此之情矣。

translations.literal: ” Those who heard in the tribe did not know truth from falsehood; some sought shelter in Bahai’s dwelling, some in Shizu’s; Shizu thus fully learned the inclinations of his brothers and followers on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: ” No one knew if the alarm was real. Some ran to Bahai’s house, others to Shizu’s—and Shizu learned exactly who stood where.

sentences.zh: 間數年，烏春來攻，世祖拒之。

translations.literal: Some years later Wuchun came to attack; Shizu resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Wuchun attacked; Shizu met him in the field.

sentences.zh: 時十月已半，大雨累晝夜，冰澌覆地，烏春不能進。

translations.literal: It was already mid-tenth month; heavy rain continued day and night; slush ice covered the ground; Wuchun could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: It was mid-tenth month. Rain fell day and night, slush ice sheeted the ground, and Wuchun could not move.

sentences.zh: 既而悔曰：「此天也！

translations.literal: Presently he repented, saying, “This is Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: At last he cried, “This is Heaven’s doing!

sentences.zh: 」乃引兵去。

translations.literal: ” Then he withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: ” and pulled his army back.

sentences.zh: 烏春舍于阿里矮村滓不乃家，而以兵圍其弟勝昆于胡不村。

translations.literal: Wuchun lodged at Zibunai’s house in Ali’ai Village, while with troops he besieged his younger brother Shengkun at Hubu Village.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun quartered at Zibunai’s home in Ali’ai village while his men besieged his brother Shengkun at Hubu village.

sentences.zh: 兵退，勝昆執其兄滓不乃，而請蒞殺于世祖，且請免其孥戮。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, Shengkun seized his elder brother Zibunai and asked Shizu to come and execute him, and also asked that his wives and children be spared slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: After the retreat Shengkun seized his brother Zibunai and asked Shizu to come and kill him, begging that the women and children be spared.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [Shizu] assented.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達亦舉兵，遣肅宗拒之。

translations.literal: Huannan and Sanda also raised troops; [Shizu] sent Suzong to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Huannan and Sanda rose too; Shizu sent Suzong (Pure Ancestor) against them.

sentences.zh: 當是時，烏春兵在北，桓赧兵在南，其勢甚盛。

translations.literal: At this time Wuchun’s army was in the north and Huannan’s in the south; their strength was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun’s force held the north and Huannan’s the south; together they were overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 戒之曰：「可和則與之和，否則決戰！

translations.literal: [Shizu] admonished him: “If peace is possible, make peace; if not, fight it out!
translations.idiomatic: He told Suzong, “Treat if you can; otherwise fight to the finish!

sentences.zh: 」肅宗兵敗。

translations.literal: ” Suzong’s army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: ” Suzong was beaten.

sentences.zh: 會烏春以久雨解去，世祖乃以偏師涉舍很水，經貼割水，覆桓赧、散達之家。

translations.literal: When Wuchun withdrew on account of the long rain, Shizu with a detached force crossed the Shehen River, passed by the Tiege River, and overthrew the households of Huannan and Sanda.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchun quit in the rains, Shizu took a flying column across the Shehen, by the Tiege, and raided Huannan and Sanda’s homes.

sentences.zh: 明日，大霧晦冥，失道，至婆多吐水乃覺。

translations.literal: Next day great fog darkened everything; they lost the way and only realized it when they reached the Potuotuo River.
translations.idiomatic: Next day fog shut out the sky; they lost the trail and only knew it when they hit the Potuotuo River.

sentences.zh: 即還至舍很、貼割之間，升高阜望之，見六騎來，大呼，馳擊之。

translations.literal: They then returned to the space between Shehen and Tiege, climbed a high mound to look, saw six horsemen coming, shouted loudly, and galloped to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: They doubled back between Shehen and Tiege, climbed a knoll, saw six riders, yelled, and charged.

sentences.zh: 世祖射一人斃，生獲五人，問之，乃知卜灰、撒骨出使助恆赧、散達者也。

translations.literal: Shizu shot one dead, captured five alive; on questioning them he learned they were envoys of Buhui and Saguchu sent to aid Huannan and Sanda.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu shot one dead and took five alive. They were envoys from Buhui and Saguchu, sent to help Huannan and Sanda.

sentences.zh: 世祖至桓赧、散達所居，焚蕩其室家。

translations.literal: Shizu reached where Huannan and Sanda dwelt and burned and swept away their houses.
translations.idiomatic: At Huannan and Sanda’s seat he burned their compounds clean.

sentences.zh: 殺百許人，舊將主保亦死之。

translations.literal: He killed on the order of a hundred men; the old general Zhuba also died in it.
translations.idiomatic: About a hundred were killed, including the veteran Zhuba.

sentences.zh: 比世祖還，與肅宗會，肅宗兵又敗矣。

translations.literal: By the time Shizu returned and met Suzong, Suzong’s army had been defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu rejoined Suzong, Suzong had lost again.

sentences.zh: 世祖讓肅宗失利之狀。

translations.literal: Shizu reproached Suzong for his losses.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu rebuked Suzong for the defeats.

sentences.zh: 遣人議和，桓赧、散達曰：「以爾盈歌之大赤馬、辭不失之紫騮馬與我，我則和。

translations.literal: He sent men to negotiate peace; Huannan and Sanda said, “Give us your Yingge’s great sorrel and Cibushi’s purple bay, and we will make peace.
translations.idiomatic: He sent to treat for peace. Huannan and Sanda demanded Yingge’s great sorrel and Cibushi’s purple bay—“then we make peace.

sentences.zh: 」二馬皆女直名馬，不許。

translations.literal: ” Both horses were famed Jurchen steeds; [Shizu] did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: ” Both were famous Jurchen horses; Shizu refused.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達大會諸部來攻，過裴滿部，以其附于世祖也，縱火焚之。

translations.literal: Huannan and Sanda gathered the tribes in great assembly to attack; passing the Puman tribe, because they had attached themselves to Shizu, they set fire and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: Huannan and Sanda mustered the tribes and marched. At the Puman, who had sided with Shizu, they fired the villages.

sentences.zh: 蒲察部沙祇勃堇、胡補答勃堇使阿喜來告難，世祖使之詭從以自全，曰：「戰則以旗鼓自別。

translations.literal: The Pucha sub-chiefs Shazhi and Hubuda sent Axi to report distress; Shizu had them feign submission to save themselves, saying, “In battle distinguish yourselves by flags and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha chiefs Shazhi and Hubuda sent Axi for help. Shizu told them to pretend loyalty and mark themselves with flags and drums in the fight.

sentences.zh: 」世祖往禦桓赧之衆，將行，有報者曰：「跋黑食於愛妾之父家，肉脹咽死矣！

translations.literal: ” As Shizu went to meet Huannan’s host, about to set out, a messenger reported, “Bahai was eating at his favorite concubine’s father’s house and choked to death on swollen flesh!
translations.idiomatic: ” As Shizu marched against Huannan, word came: “Bahai feasted at his concubine’s father’s house and choked on meat—dead!

sentences.zh: 」乃遣肅宗求援於遼，遂率衆出。

translations.literal: ” He thereupon sent Suzong to seek aid from Liao and led the host out.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent Suzong to beg Liao for aid and led the army out himself.

sentences.zh: 使辭不失取海姑兄弟兵，已而乃知海姑兄弟貳於桓赧矣。

translations.literal: He sent Cibushi to fetch the troops of the Haigu brothers; presently he learned the Haigu brothers had turned to Huannan.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Cibushi to raise the Haigu brothers’ men, then learned they had gone over to Huannan.

sentences.zh: 欲並取其衆，徑至海姑。

translations.literal: Wishing to seize their forces as well, he went straight to Haigu.
translations.idiomatic: Intent on taking them in one stroke, he pushed straight to Haigu.

sentences.zh: 偵者報曰：「敵已至。

translations.literal: Scouts reported, “The enemy has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts cried, “The enemy is here!

sentences.zh: 」將戰，世祖戒辭不失曰：「汝先陣於脫豁改原，待吾三揚旗，三鳴鼓，即棄旗決戰。

translations.literal: ” About to fight, Shizu charged Cibushi: “Take position first on the Tohuogai plain; when I raise the flag three times and beat the drum three times, cast aside the flag and fight to the decision.
translations.idiomatic: ” Before battle Shizu told Cibushi, “Hold the Tohuogai plain. When I raise the banner thrice and beat the drum thrice, drop the flag and charge.

sentences.zh: 死生惟在今日，命不足惜！

translations.literal: Life and death hang on this day alone; life is not to be cherished!
translations.idiomatic: Today decides all—do not spare your lives!

sentences.zh: 」使裴滿胡喜牽大紫騮馬以爲貳馬，馳至陣。

translations.literal: ” He had Puman Huxi lead the great purple-bay horse as a spare mount and galloped to the line.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had Puman Huxi bring the great purple-bay as a remount and rode to the front.

sentences.zh: 時桓赧、散達盛強，世祖軍吏未戰而懼，皆植立無人色。

translations.literal: At this time Huannan and Sanda were in full strength; Shizu’s officers, before fighting, were afraid—all stood rooted, without color in their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Huannan and Sanda were at their peak. Shizu’s officers had not yet fought and already looked like corpses on their feet.

sentences.zh: 世祖陽陽如平常，亦無責讓之言，但令士卒解甲少憩，以水沃面，調蒨水飲之。

translations.literal: Shizu was as calm and easy as on ordinary days; there was neither blame nor rebuke; he only ordered the soldiers to remove armor and rest a little, wash their faces with water, and mix madder water for them to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu seemed unhurried as ever—no scolding—only told the men to unarm, rest, splash water on their faces, and drink madder tea.

sentences.zh: 有頃，訓勵之，軍勢復振。

translations.literal: After a while, having exhorted them, military spirit revived.
translations.idiomatic: A short rallying speech, and the ranks steadied.

sentences.zh: 乃避衆獨引穆宗，執其手密與之言曰：「今日之事，若勝則已，萬一有不勝，吾必無生。

translations.literal: He then withdrew from the crowd and led Muzong aside alone, took his hand and spoke to him secretly: “Today’s affair—if we win, that is all; if by any chance we do not win, I shall surely not live.
translations.idiomatic: He drew Muzong (Tranquil Ancestor) aside, gripped his hand, and whispered: “If we win, well. If we lose, I will not come back.

sentences.zh: 汝今介馬遙觀，勿預戰事。

translations.literal: You now, with a spare horse, observe from afar; do not take part in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Keep a spare horse and watch from a distance—stay out of the fight.

sentences.zh: 若我死，汝勿收吾骨，勿顧戀親戚，亟馳馬奔告汝兄頗剌淑，於遼系籍受印，乞師以報此仇！

translations.literal: If I die, do not collect my bones, do not linger over kinsmen; swiftly gallop to tell your elder brother Polasu—enter Liao registration and receive the seal, beg troops to avenge this grudge!”
translations.idiomatic: If I fall, leave my body, forget kin, ride to your brother Polasu—take Liao registration and a seal, and beg an army for revenge!”

sentences.zh: 」語畢，袒袖，不被甲，以縕袍垂襴護前後心，韔弓提劍，三揚旗，三鳴鼓，棄旗搏戰，身爲軍鋒，突入敵陣，衆從之。

translations.literal: When the words were finished, he bared his arms, wore no armor, used a padded gown with hanging flaps to protect heart and back, bow in case and sword in hand; three times he raised the flag, three times beat the drum, cast aside the flag and grappled in battle; his person was the army’s spear-point, bursting into the enemy formation, and the masses followed.
translations.idiomatic: He rolled his sleeves, wore no mail, only a quilted coat with skirts guarding chest and back, bow slung and sword drawn; thrice he raised the banner, thrice the drum, then threw the flag down and led the charge himself into the enemy line—and the host followed.

sentences.zh: 辭不失從後奮擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Cibushi struck fiercely from the rear, and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Cibushi hammered from behind and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐之，自阿不彎至於北隘甸，死者如僕麻，破多吐水水爲之赤，棄車甲馬牛軍實盡獲之。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory they pursued them from Abuwan to Beiaidian; the dead lay thick as hemp stalks, the Poduotu waters ran red, and abandoned chariots, armor, horses, cattle, and military stores were all taken.
translations.idiomatic: They chased the rout from Abuwan to Beiaidian. Corpses carpeted the ground like cut hemp; the Poduotu ran red. Chariots, mail, horses, oxen, and all war stores left behind were seized.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「今日之捷，非天不能及此，亦可以知足矣。

translations.literal: Shizu said: “Today’s victory—without Heaven one could not reach this; one may also be content.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu said, “Heaven alone gave us a victory like this—we have reason to be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 雖縱之去，敗軍之氣，沒世不振。

translations.literal: Though we let them go, the spirit of a defeated army will not revive in a lifetime.”
translations.idiomatic: Even if we let them escape, a beaten army’s morale will never recover.”

sentences.zh: 」乃引軍還。

translations.literal: ” Then he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then withdrew the host.

sentences.zh: 世祖視其戰地，馳突成大路，闊且三十隴。

translations.literal: Shizu surveyed the battlefield; the charges had worn a great road, wide as thirty ridge-lines.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu walked the field of battle. Cavalry charges had trampled a highway thirty ridges wide.

sentences.zh: 手殺九人，自相重積，人皆異之。

translations.literal: With his own hand he had killed nine men; they lay piled upon one another, and all marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: He had personally slain nine men, bodies heaped one on another—a feat men spoke of with awe.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達自此不能復聚，未幾，各以其屬來降，遼大安七年也。

translations.literal: Huanzan and Sanda could not rally again; before long each came to submit with his followers—it was Liao Da’an year seven.
translations.idiomatic: Huanzan and Sanda never regrouped. Soon each arrived with his following to surrender. It was Liao Da’an year seven (1091).

sentences.zh: 初，桓赧兄弟之變，不术魯部卜灰、蒲察部撒骨出助之。

translations.literal: At first, in the revolt of the Huanzan brothers, Buqi of the Bushilu tribe and Saguchu of the Pucha tribe had aided them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huanzan brothers first rebelled, Buqi of the Bushilu and Saguchu of the Pucha had backed them.

sentences.zh: 至是，招之，不肯和。

translations.literal: At this time they were summoned but would not make peace.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shizu called them in, but they refused terms.

sentences.zh: 卜灰之党石魯遂殺卜灰來降。

translations.literal: Shilu of Buqi’s faction then killed Buqi and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu, of Buqi’s party, killed Buqi and defected.

sentences.zh: 撒骨出追躡亡者，道傍人潛射之，中口而死。

translations.literal: Saguchu pursued fugitives; someone by the road shot him in secret, struck the mouth, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Saguchu chased stragglers. A man beside the road loosed a hidden arrow into his mouth and killed him.

sentences.zh: 自是舊部悉歸。

translations.literal: From this time all the old followers returned.
translations.idiomatic: After that the old adherents all came back.

sentences.zh: 景祖時，斡勒部人杯乃來屬，及是，有他志。

translations.literal: In Jingzu’s time Beinai of the Wale tribe had come to submit; by now he harbored other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingzu, Beinai of the Wale had submitted; now he turned disloyal.

sentences.zh: 會其家失火，因以縱火誣歡部，世祖征償如約。

translations.literal: When his house caught fire he falsely accused the Huan tribe of arson; Shizu exacted compensation as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: His dwelling burned; he blamed the Huan for setting the fire. Shizu levied the indemnity the compact required.

sentences.zh: 杯乃不自安，遂結烏春、窩謀罕舉兵。

translations.literal: Beinai felt insecure and thereupon joined Wuchun and Womouhan in raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Beinai allied with Wuchun and Womouhan and took up arms.

sentences.zh: 使肅宗與戰，敗之，獲杯乃，世祖獻之於遼。

translations.literal: He had Suzong fight them, defeated them, and captured Beinai; Shizu presented him to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong was sent against them, won, and took Beinai prisoner. Shizu handed him over to the Liao.

sentences.zh: 臘醅、麻產侵掠野居女直，略來流水牧馬。

translations.literal: Lapai and Machan raided the wild Jurchen and drove off horses pastured at Liushui.
translations.idiomatic: Lapai and Machan harried the wild Jurchen and lifted horses from the Liushui pastures.

sentences.zh: 世祖擊之，中四創，久之疾愈。

translations.literal: Shizu attacked them, received four wounds, and after a long while recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu struck them, took four wounds, and was slow to heal.

sentences.zh: 臘醅等復略穆宗牧馬，交結諸部。

translations.literal: Lapai and the rest again drove off Muzong’s horses and won over other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Lapai’s band raided Muzong’s herds again and drew other tribes into alliance.

sentences.zh: 世祖復伐之，臘醅等紿降，乃旋。

translations.literal: Shizu campaigned against them again; Lapai and the rest feigned submission, and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu marched once more; Lapai pretended to yield, and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 臘醅得姑里甸兵百十有七人，據暮稜水守險，石顯子婆諸刊亦在其中。

translations.literal: Lapai had obtained a hundred and seventeen soldiers from Guli and held the defiles along the Muleng River; Shi Xian’s son Pojukan was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Lapai mustered a hundred and seventeen Guli fighters, fortified the Muleng, and Pojukan, son of Shi Xian, stood with him.

sentences.zh: 世祖圍而克之，盡獲姑里甸兵。

translations.literal: Shizu besieged and took them and captured all the Guli soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu invested the position, broke it, and took every Guli man.

sentences.zh: 麻產遁去。

translations.literal: Machan escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Machan got away.

sentences.zh: 遂擒臘醅及婆諸刊，皆獻之遼。

translations.literal: He then seized Lapai and Pojukan and presented both to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Lapai and Pojukan were seized and sent up to the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 既已，復請之，遼人與之，並以前後所獻罪人歸之。

translations.literal: Afterward he requested them back; the Liao returned them, together with all criminals previously presented.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked the Liao to return them—and received them, with every captive he had earlier sent, back in his hands.

sentences.zh: 歡都在破烏春等於斜堆，故石、拔石皆就擒。

translations.literal: Huandou had broken Wuchun and the rest at Xiedui, and Gushi and Bashi were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: Huandou had routed Wuchun at Xiedui; Gushi and Bashi were taken there.

sentences.zh: 世祖自將與歡都合兵嶺東，諸軍皆至。

translations.literal: Shizu personally led troops to join Huandou east of the passes, and all the armies assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu took the field in person, joined Huandou beyond the eastern ridges, and the hosts gathered.

sentences.zh: 是時，烏春已前死，窩謀罕請於遼，願和解。

translations.literal: By this time Wuchun was already dead; Womouhan petitioned Liao, wishing to make peace.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun was already dead. Womouhan appealed to the Liao for a settlement.

sentences.zh: 既與和，復來襲，乃進軍圍之。

translations.literal: After peace was made they attacked again; he thereupon advanced and besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: No sooner was peace sworn than they struck again; he marched up and laid siege.

sentences.zh: 窩謀罕棄城遁去。

translations.literal: Womouhan abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Womouhan deserted the town and ran.

sentences.zh: 破其城，盡俘獲之，以功差次分賜諸軍。

translations.literal: The city was stormed and all were captured; spoils were distributed to the armies in order of merit.
translations.idiomatic: The place fell; every defender was taken. Booty was parceled out by rank of service.

sentences.zh: 城始破，議渠長生殺，衆皆長跪，遼使者在坐。

translations.literal: When the city had just fallen they debated whether to kill the chieftains; the multitude all knelt long, and a Liao envoy sat present.
translations.idiomatic: As the walls gave way they argued over executing the headmen. The men knelt in ranks while a Liao envoy looked on.

sentences.zh: 忽一人佩長刀突前咫尺，謂世祖曰：「勿殺我！

translations.literal: Suddenly a man wearing a long sword rushed within a foot of him and said to Shizu: “Do not kill me!
translations.idiomatic: A warrior with a long blade suddenly lunged to within a pace of Shizu and cried, “Spare me!

sentences.zh: 」遼使及左右皆走匿。

translations.literal: ” The Liao envoy and attendants all fled to hide.
translations.idiomatic: ” The envoy and guards scattered in panic.

sentences.zh: 世祖色不少動，執其人之手，語之曰：「吾不殺汝也。

translations.literal: Shizu’s expression did not shift; he grasped the man’s hand and said to him: “I will not kill you.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu never flinched. He caught the man’s wrist and said, “I will not kill you.

sentences.zh: 」於是罰左右匿者，曰：「汝等何敢失次耶？

translations.literal: ” He then punished those who had hidden, saying: “How dare you break ranks?
translations.idiomatic: ” Then he punished the men who had bolted: “Who gave you leave to break formation?

sentences.zh: 」罰既已，乃徐使執突前者殺之。

translations.literal: ” When the punishment was finished, he slowly had them seize the man who had rushed forward and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: ” When discipline was done, he calmly ordered the rushers seized—and the man put to death.

sentences.zh: 其膽勇鎮物如此。

translations.literal: Such was his courage in subduing others.
translations.idiomatic: So steady was the nerve with which he mastered men.

sentences.zh: 師還，寢疾，遂篤。

translations.literal: The army returned; he took to his bed ill, and the illness grew grave.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home he fell sick, and the sickness turned mortal.

sentences.zh: 元娶拏懶氏哭不止，世祖曰：「汝勿哭，汝惟後我一歲耳。

translations.literal: His primary wife, Lady Nalan, wept without cease; Shizu said: “Do not weep—you are but one year behind me.
translations.idiomatic: His chief wife Lady Nalan would not stop crying. Shizu said, “Enough—you will follow me by only a year.

sentences.zh: 」肅宗請後事，曰：「汝惟後我三年。

translations.literal: ” Suzong asked about affairs after his death; he said: “You are but three years behind me.
translations.idiomatic: ” Suzong asked what should be done when he was gone. “You—three years,” he said.

sentences.zh: 」肅宗出，謂人曰：「吾兄至此，亦不與我好言。

translations.literal: ” Suzong went out and told others: “My elder brother even now will not speak kindly to me.
translations.idiomatic: ” Suzong left the tent and said to those outside, “Even dying, my brother gives me no kind word.

sentences.zh: 」乃叩地而哭。

translations.literal: ” Then he beat the ground and wept.
translations.idiomatic: ” He struck the earth with his forehead and sobbed.

sentences.zh: 俄呼穆宗謂曰：「烏雅束柔善，若辦集契丹事，阿骨打能之。

translations.literal: Soon he called Muzong and said to him: “Wuyashu is gentle; if one must manage Khitan affairs, Aguda can do it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon summoned Muzong. “Wuyashu is mild,” he said. “For Khitan business, Aguda is the man.

sentences.zh: 」遼大安八年五月十五日卒。

translations.literal: ” He died on the fifteenth day of the fifth month, Liao Da’an year eight.
translations.idiomatic: ” He died on the fifteenth day of the fifth month of Liao Da’an year eight (1092).

sentences.zh: 襲位十九年，年五十四。

translations.literal: He had held the succession nineteen years; his age was fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He had ruled nineteen years and was fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 明年，拏懶氏卒。

translations.literal: The next year Lady Nalan died.
translations.idiomatic: The year after, Lady Nalan died.

sentences.zh: 又明年，肅宗卒。

translations.literal: The year after that, Suzong died.
translations.idiomatic: Another year on, Suzong died.

sentences.zh: 肅宗病篤，歎曰：「我兄真多智哉！

translations.literal: Suzong, gravely ill, sighed: “My brother was truly full of wisdom!
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Suzong sighed, “My brother saw everything!

sentences.zh: 」世祖天性嚴重，有智識，一見必識，暫聞不忘。

translations.literal: ” Shizu by nature was stern and weighty, possessed knowledge—one sight and he would recognize a man; brief hearing and he did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shizu was grave by nature and sharp of mind: one meeting and he knew a face; a word once heard, never lost.

sentences.zh: 凝寒不縮栗，動止不回顧。

translations.literal: In freezing cold he did not shiver; in movement or rest he never looked back.
translations.idiomatic: He did not flinch in bitter cold, and never glanced behind him.

sentences.zh: 每戰未嘗被甲，先以夢兆候其勝負。

translations.literal: Before each battle he never wore armor; first by dream omens he gauged victory or defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He never donned armor before a fight, trusting first to dreams to read whether he would win or lose.

sentences.zh: 嘗乘醉騎驢入室中，明日見驢足跡，問而知之，自是不復飲酒。

translations.literal: Once, drunk, he rode a donkey into the inner chamber; next day he saw donkey tracks, asked and learned of it, and from then did not drink wine again.
translations.idiomatic: Once he rode a donkey drunk into the women’s quarters. Next morning he saw the tracks, learned what he had done, and never drank again.

sentences.zh: 襲位之初，內外潰叛，締交爲寇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of succeeding to the position, inside and outside were in collapse and rebellion; those bound by friendship became foes.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his rule, kinsmen and allies rebelled, and sworn friends took up arms as enemies.

sentences.zh: 世祖乃因敗爲功，變弱爲強。

translations.literal: Shizu then turned defeat into achievement, weakness into strength.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu turned defeat to triumph and weakness to power.

sentences.zh: 既破桓赧、散達、烏春、窩謀罕，基業自此大矣。

translations.literal: Having broken Huanzan, Sanda, Wuchun, and Womouhan, the foundation from this grew great.
translations.idiomatic: After crushing Huanzan, Sanda, Wuchun, and Womouhan, the house stood on a far grander footing.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，追諡聖肅皇帝，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: In Tianhui year fifteen, posthumously titled Emperor Shensu, temple name Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year fifteen (1137) he was posthumously named Emperor Shensu, with the temple name Shizu.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏曰永陵。

translations.literal: In Huangtong year four, his burial was styled Yongling.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year four (1144) his tomb was named Yongling.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡世祖神武聖肅皇帝。

translations.literal: In year five, additional title: Shizu, divine and martial, sage and solemn emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his title was raised to Shizu, Divine Martial Sage Solemn Emperor.

sentences.zh: 母弟頗剌淑襲節度使，景祖第四子也，是爲肅宗。

translations.literal: Younger uterine brother Pulasu succeeded as military commissioner; Jingzu’s fourth son—this was Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Pulasu inherited the commissionership—Jingzu’s fourth son, known as Suzong (Pure Ancestor).

sentences.zh: 遼重熙十一年壬午歲生。

translations.literal: Born in the ren-wu year, Liao Chongxi year eleven.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the ren-wu year of Liao Chongxi (1042).

sentences.zh: 在父兄時號國相。

translations.literal: In the time of father and elder brothers he was styled Guoxiang (State Minister).
translations.idiomatic: Under his father and brothers he bore the title Guoxiang, or State Minister.

sentences.zh: 國相之稱不知始何時。

translations.literal: When the title Guoxiang began is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: No one knows when the office of Guoxiang first arose.

sentences.zh: 初，雅達爲國相。

translations.literal: At first Yada was Guoxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yada held the title first.

sentences.zh: 雅達者，桓赧、散達之父也。

translations.literal: Yada was the father of Huanzan and Sanda.
translations.idiomatic: Yada was father to Huanzan and Sanda.

sentences.zh: 景祖以幣馬求之于雅達，而命肅宗爲之。

translations.literal: Jingzu with silks and horses sought it from Yada and ordered Suzong to take the office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu bought the post from Yada with gifts and installed Suzong as Guoxiang.

sentences.zh: 肅宗自幼機敏善辯。

translations.literal: Suzong from youth was quick-witted and skilled in disputation.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong was clever and articulate from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 當其兄時，身居國相，盡心匡輔。

translations.literal: In his elder brother’s time, holding the office of Guoxiang, he devoted his heart to supporting and assisting.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizu ruled, he served as Guoxiang and gave his full support.

sentences.zh: 是時，叔父跋黑有異志，及桓赧、散達、烏春、窩謀罕、石顯父子、臘醅、麻產作難，用兵之際，肅宗屢當一面。

translations.literal: At this time his uncle Bahei harbored other ambitions, and when Huanzan, Sanda, Wuchun, Womouhan, Shi Xian father and son, Lapai, and Machan made trouble, in the campaigns Suzong repeatedly held one wing alone.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Bahei nursed other designs, and when Huanzan, Sanda, Wuchun, Womouhan, Shi Xian and his son, Lapai, and Machan rose, Suzong again and again took a front on his own.

sentences.zh: 尤能知遼人國政人情。

translations.literal: He especially understood Liao statecraft and human feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He knew Liao politics and manners better than anyone.

sentences.zh: 凡有遼事，一切委之肅宗專心焉。

translations.literal: Whatever concerned Liao affairs, all was entrusted to Suzong to handle with single-minded care.
translations.idiomatic: All business with the Liao went entirely to Suzong.

sentences.zh: 凡白事於遼官，皆令遠跪陳辭，譯者傳致之，往往爲譯者錯亂。

translations.literal: Whenever reporting matters to Liao officials, all were made to kneel at a distance and state their case; translators conveyed it—often the translators garbled things.
translations.idiomatic: Petitioners before Liao officials had to kneel far off while interpreters relayed their words—and the interpreters often mangled the plea.

sentences.zh: 肅宗欲得自前委曲言之，故先不以實告譯者。

translations.literal: Suzong wished to come forward himself and explain in detail, so at first he did not tell the translators the full truth.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong wanted to speak face to face in full, so he deliberately kept the interpreters in the dark.

sentences.zh: 譯者惑之，不得已，引之前，使自言。

translations.literal: The translators were perplexed; having no choice, they led him forward to speak for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Baffled, the interpreters at last brought him before the officials to speak in person.

sentences.zh: 乃以草木瓦石爲籌，枚數其事而陳之。

translations.literal: He then used grass, wood, tiles, and stones as counters, counting off each item of business as he presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out twigs, pebbles, and shards as tallies and walked the officials through each point of his case.

sentences.zh: 官吏聽者皆愕然，問其故，則爲卑辭以對曰：「鄙陋無文，故如此。

translations.literal: The listening officials were all startled; asked the reason, he answered with humble words: “I am crude and without learning, therefore thus.”
translations.idiomatic: The clerks stared. Asked why he did so, he answered meekly, “I am a rude man without book learning—that is why.”

sentences.zh: 」官吏以爲實然，不復疑之，是以所訴無不如意。

translations.literal: ” The officials took it as sincere and no longer suspected him; thus nothing he pleaded failed to win its wish.
translations.idiomatic: ” They took him at his word and never doubted him again; from then on every suit he brought succeeded.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達之戰，部人賽罕死之，其弟活羅陰懷忿怨。

translations.literal: In the war with Huanzan and Sanda, the tribesman Saihan died; his younger brother Huoluo secretly nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Huanzan and Sanda the clansman Saihan was killed; his brother Huoluo brooded on revenge.

sentences.zh: 一日，忽以劍脊置肅宗項上曰：「吾兄爲汝輩死矣！

translations.literal: One day he suddenly placed the spine of his sword on Suzong’s neck and said: “My brother died for you people!
translations.idiomatic: One day he set the flat of his blade on Suzong’s neck and cried, “My brother died for your sake!

sentences.zh: 剄汝以償，則如之何？

translations.literal: To cut your throat in payment—what then?
translations.idiomatic: If I slit your throat to pay him back—what then?

sentences.zh: 」久之，因其兄柩至，遂怒而攻習不出，習不出走避之。

translations.literal: ” After long time, because his brother’s coffin arrived, he flew into rage and attacked Xibuchu; Xibuchu fled to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Months later, when his brother’s bier came home, he turned on Xibuchu in fury; Xibuchu ran.

sentences.zh: 攻肅宗於家，矢注次室之裙，著於門扉。

translations.literal: He attacked Suzong at home; an arrow pinned the skirt of the side chamber, embedding in the door panel.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Suzong’s house. An arrow pierced a side room’s curtain and stood quivering in the doorframe.

sentences.zh: 復攻歡都，歡都衷甲拒於室中，既不能入，持其門旃而去，往附杯乃。

translations.literal: Again he attacked Huandu; Huandu wore armor inside the room and barred entry; unable to enter, [Huoluo] seized his door-banner and left, going to join Beinai.
translations.idiomatic: He next attacked Huandu, who armored inside and barred the door. Foiled, Huoluo snatched Huandu’s door pennant and fled to Beinai.

sentences.zh: 杯乃誘烏春兵度嶺，世祖與遇于蘇素海甸。

translations.literal: Beinai lured Wuchun’s troops over the pass; Shizu met them at the Susu Sea meadow.
translations.idiomatic: Beinai drew Wuchun’s men over the ridge. Shizu met them on the Susu Sea meadow.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「予昔有異夢，今不可親戰。

translations.literal: Shizu said: “I once had a strange dream; today I cannot fight in person.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu said, “I dreamed an omen once—today I must not fight myself.

sentences.zh: 若左軍中有力戰者，則大功成矣！

translations.literal: If in the left wing there is one who fights hard, the great achievement will be complete!
translations.idiomatic: If someone on the left will strike hard, the day is won!

sentences.zh: 」命肅宗及斜列、辭不失與之戰。

translations.literal: ” He ordered Suzong, Xielie, and Cibushi to fight them.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent Suzong, Xielie, and Cibushi against them.

sentences.zh: 肅宗下馬，名呼世祖，復自呼其名而言曰：「若天助我當爲衆部長，則今日之事神祇監之。

translations.literal: Suzong dismounted, called Shizu by name, then called his own name and said: “If Heaven aids me to become chief of all the tribes, then today’s affair the spirits witness.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong dismounted, hailed Shizu by name, then his own, and vowed, “If Heaven makes me chief of all the tribes, let the spirits witness this day.

sentences.zh: 」語畢再拜。
