translations.literal: ” When the words were finished, he bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: ” He bowed twice and rose.

sentences.zh: 遂炷火束縕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he kindled fire and bound kindling.
translations.idiomatic: Then he lit a fire and bound bundles of dry grass.

sentences.zh: 頃之，大風自後起，火益熾。

translations.literal: Presently a great wind rose from behind; the fire blazed fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a strong wind rose at their backs and the flames leapt higher.

sentences.zh: 是時八月，並青草皆焚之，煙焰漲天。

translations.literal: It was then the eighth month; all the green grass was burnt; smoke and flame swelled to the sky.
translations.idiomatic: It was the eighth month; the blaze took the standing grass and smoke filled the sky.

sentences.zh: 我軍隨煙衝擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Our army followed the smoke and charged; utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Our men charged through the smoke and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 遂獲杯乃，囚而獻諸遼。

translations.literal: Thereupon they captured Beinai, imprisoned him, and presented him to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Beinai was taken, bound, and sent up to the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 並獲活羅，肅宗釋其罪，左右任使之，後竟得其力焉。

translations.literal: They also captured Huoluo; Suzong released his guilt, kept him close at hand and employed him—and in the end indeed gained his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Huoluo was taken too. Suzong pardoned him, kept him at his side, and in time won his loyal service.

sentences.zh: 大安八年，自國相襲位。

translations.literal: In Da’an year eight, from Guoxiang he succeeded to the position.
translations.idiomatic: In Da’an year eight (1092) he inherited rule from his post as Guoxiang.

sentences.zh: 是時，麻產尚據直屋鎧水，繕完營堡，誘納亡命。

translations.literal: At this time Machan still held Zhiwu on the Kai River, repaired fortifications, and enticed fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Machan still held Zhiwu on the Kai River, rebuilt his forts, and sheltered outlaws.

sentences.zh: 招之，不聽，遣康宗伐之。

translations.literal: [Suzong] summoned him; he would not heed, and sent Kangzong to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong called him in; he refused. Kangzong was sent against him.

sentences.zh: 太祖別軍取麻產家屬，錡釜無遺。

translations.literal: Taizu with a separate force took Machan’s household; not a pot or cauldron was left.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu (Grand Ancestor) took a detachment and seized Machan’s family—every kettle carried off.

sentences.zh: 既獲麻產，殺之，獻馘於遼。

translations.literal: Having captured Machan, he killed him and presented the severed ears to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Machan was taken, executed, and his ears sent to the Liao as trophy.

sentences.zh: 陶溫水民來附。

translations.literal: The people of Tao Wen water came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Tao Wen River clans came over in submission.

sentences.zh: 二年癸酉，遣太祖以偏師伐泥厖古部帥水抹離海村跋黑、播立開，平之，自是寇賊皆息。

translations.literal: In year two, guiyou, he sent Taizu with a flank army to attack Nimogu division chief Shuimoli, Haicun Bagehei, and Bolikai; he pacified them, and from this time bandits and rebels all quieted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, guiyou (1093), Taizu was sent with a detachment against the Nimogu chief Shuimoli, Haicun Bagehei, and Bolikai. They were subdued, and raiding ceased from then on.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，肅宗卒。

translations.literal: In year three, the eighth month, Suzong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, in the eighth month, Suzong died.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，追諡穆憲皇帝。

translations.literal: In Tianhui year fifteen, posthumously titled Emperor Muzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year fifteen (1137) he was posthumously named Emperor Muzhen (Solemn and Virtuous).

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，藏號泰陵。

translations.literal: In Huangtong year four, burial styled Tailing.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year four (1144) his tomb was named Tailing.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡肅宗明睿穆憲皇帝。

translations.literal: In year five, additional title: Suzong, bright and sage, solemn and virtuous emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his title was raised to Suzong, Bright and Sage Solemn and Virtuous Emperor.

sentences.zh: 母弟穆宗，諱盈歌，字烏魯完，景祖第五子也。

translations.literal: Younger uterine brother Muzong, taboo name Yingge, style Wuluwan, was Jingzu’s fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Muzong (Tranquil Ancestor), taboo name Yingge, style Wuluwan, was Jingzu’s fifth son.

sentences.zh: 南人稱揚割太師，又曰揚割追諡孝平皇帝，號穆宗，又曰揚割號仁祖。

translations.literal: Southerners call him Grand Preceptor Yangge; they also say Yangge was posthumously titled Emperor Xiaoping, with the reign title Muzong; they also say Yangge was titled Renzu.
translations.idiomatic: Southern writers call him Grand Preceptor Yangge, posthumous Emperor Xiaoping, reign title Muzong—or even Renzu (Benevolent Ancestor).

sentences.zh: 金代無號仁祖者，穆宗諱盈歌，諡孝平，「盈」近「揚」，「歌」近「割」，南北音訛。

translations.literal: The Jin had no ruler titled Renzu. Muzong’s taboo was Yingge and his posthumous name Xiaoping; “ying” approximates “yang,” and “ge” approximates “ge” (to cut)—a north–south phonetic corruption.
translations.idiomatic: No Jin ruler was ever called Renzu. Muzong was Yingge, posthumously Xiaoping; “ying” sounds like “yang” and “ge” like “ge” (to cut)—a southern mishearing.

sentences.zh: 遼人呼節度使爲太師，自景祖至太祖皆有是稱。

translations.literal: The Liao called the military commissioner Grand Preceptor; from Jingzu through Taizu all bore this title.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao styled the military commissioner “Grand Preceptor”; every chief from Jingzu to Taizu used it.

sentences.zh: 凡《叢言》、《松漠記》、張棣《金志》等書皆無足取。

translations.literal: All books such as Congyan, Songmo ji, and Zhang Di’s Jin zhi are not worth taking up.
translations.idiomatic: Works like Congyan, Songmo ji, and Zhang Di’s Jin zhi are not to be trusted.

sentences.zh: 穆宗，遼重熙二十二年癸巳歲生。

translations.literal: Muzong was born in Liao Chongxi year twenty-two, the guisi year.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong was born in Liao Chongxi year twenty-two, guisi (1053).

sentences.zh: 肅宗時擒麻產，遼命穆宗爲詳穩。

translations.literal: When Suzong captured Machan, the Liao appointed Muzong xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzong took Machan, the Liao made Muzong a xiangwen (detachment commander).

sentences.zh: 大安十年甲戌，襲節度使，年四十二。

translations.literal: In Da’an year ten, jiaxu, he inherited the military commissionership, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Da’an year ten, jiaxu (1094), he inherited the commissionership, aged forty-two.

sentences.zh: 以兄劾者子撒改爲國相。

translations.literal: He made Hezhe’s son Sagai state minister.
translations.idiomatic: He installed Hezhe’s son Sagai as Guoxiang (State Minister).

sentences.zh: 三年丙子，唐括部跋葛勃堇與溫都部人跋忒有舊，跋葛以事往，跋忒殺跋葛。

translations.literal: In year three, bingzi, Tangguo division’s Bagehejin and Wendu division’s Bate had an old bond; Bage went on business, and Bate killed Bage.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, bingzi (1096), Bagehejin of the Tangguo and Bate of the Wendu were old friends. Bagehejin went on a visit; Bate killed him.

sentences.zh: 使太祖率師伐跋忒，跋忒亡去，追及，殺之星顯水，紇石烈部阿疏、毛睹祿阻兵爲難，穆宗自將伐阿疏，撒改以偏師攻鈍恩城，拔之。

translations.literal: He sent Taizu to lead troops against Bate; Bate fled, was pursued and killed at Xingxian River. Heishilie division Ashu and Maoduilu blocked the road with arms and made trouble. Muzong personally led the attack on Ashu; Sagai with a flank army attacked Dun’en city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was sent against Bate, who fled and was run down and killed at Xingxian River. Ashu and Maoduilu of the Heishilie barred the way with force. Muzong marched in person on Ashu while Sagai took a detachment, stormed Dun’en, and carried the town.

sentences.zh: 阿疏初聞來伐，乃自訴於遼。

translations.literal: Ashu, on first hearing of the expedition, appealed to the Liao himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashu heard they were coming, he fled to the Liao court to plead his case.

sentences.zh: 遂留劾者守阿疏城，穆宗乃還。

translations.literal: He then left Hezhe to hold Ashu city, and Muzong returned.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong left Hezhe to hold Ashu’s stronghold and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會陶溫水、徒籠古水紇石烈部阿閣版及石魯阻五國鷹路，執殺遼捕鷹使者。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Heishilie of Tao Wen water and Tulungu water—Akeban and Shilu—blocked the Five States hawk-road and seized and killed Liao hawk envoys.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Akeban and Shilu of the Tao Wen and Tulungu Heishilie cut the Five States hawk-road and murdered Liao falconers.

sentences.zh: 遼詔穆宗討之，阿閣版等據險立柵。

translations.literal: The Liao ordered Muzong to punish them; Akeban and the rest held defiles and built palisades.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao ordered Muzong against them. Akeban’s men held the passes and threw up stockades.

sentences.zh: 方大寒，乃募善射者操勁弓利矢攻之。

translations.literal: It was bitter cold; he recruited skilled archers with stiff bows and sharp arrows to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In deep winter he raised marksmen with heavy bows and drove the attack.

sentences.zh: 數日，入其城，出遼使存者數人，俾之歸。

translations.literal: After several days they entered the city, found several surviving Liao envoys, and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the town fell. A few Liao envoys still alive were found and sent back.

sentences.zh: 統門、渾蠢水之交烏古論部留可、詐都與蘇濱水烏古論敵庫德，起兵于米里迷石罕城，納根涅之子鈍恩亦亡去，於是兩黨作難。

translations.literal: At the junction of Tongmen and Hunchun waters, Wugulun division’s Liuke and Zhadou, with Supin River Wugulun Dikude, raised troops at Mili Mishihan city; Nagenie’s son Dun’en also fled. Thus the two factions made trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Where Tongmen and Hunchun meet, Liuke and Zhadou of the Wugulun, with Dikude of the Supin Wugulun, rose at Mili Mishihan. Nagenie’s son Dun’en fled too, and two rebel camps formed.

sentences.zh: 八月，撒改爲都統，辭不失、阿里合懣、斡帶副之，以伐留可、詐都、塢塔等。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Sagai became commander-in-chief, with Cibushi, Ali Hemun, and Wodai as deputies, to attack Liuke, Zhadou, Wuta, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Sagai took overall command, with Cibushi, Ali Hemun, and Wodai as lieutenants, to crush Liuke, Zhadou, Wuta, and their allies.

sentences.zh: 謾都訶、石土門伐敵庫德。

translations.literal: Manduhu and Shitumen attacked Dikude.
translations.idiomatic: Manduhu and Shitumen moved against Dikude.

sentences.zh: 撒改欲先平邊地城堡，或欲先取留可，莫能決，乃命太祖往。

translations.literal: Sagai wished first to pacify the border castles, or first to take Liuke; unable to decide, he ordered Taizu to go.
translations.idiomatic: Sagai could not choose between clearing the border forts or striking Liuke first and sent Taizu to settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 鈍恩將援留可，乘謾都訶兵未集而攻之。

translations.literal: Dun’en was about to aid Liuke; he attacked while Manduhu’s troops were not yet assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Dun’en meant to relieve Liuke and struck before Manduhu’s men had gathered.

sentences.zh: 石土門軍既與謾都訶會，迎擊鈍恩，大敗之，降米里迷石罕城，獲鈍恩、敵庫德，釋弗殺。

translations.literal: Shitumen’s army having joined Manduhu, they met and attacked Dun’en, utterly defeated him, took Mili Mishihan city, and captured Dun’en and Dikude but did not kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Shitumen linked with Manduhu, met Dun’en, and broke him. Mili Mishihan fell; Dun’en and Dikude were taken alive and spared.

sentences.zh: 太祖度盆搦嶺，與撒改會，攻破留可城，留可已先往遼矣，盡殺其城中渠長。

translations.literal: Taizu crossed Pennao ridge, joined Sagai, and stormed Liuke’s city. Liuke had already gone to the Liao; they killed all the leaders in the city.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu crossed Pennao ridge, united with Sagai, and took Liuke’s town. Liuke had already fled to the Liao; every chief in the place was put to death.

sentences.zh: 還圍塢塔城，塢塔先已亡在外，城降於軍。

translations.literal: On the return they besieged Wuta’s city. Wuta had already fled outside; the city surrendered to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Turning back, they invested Wuta’s stronghold. Wuta was gone; the garrison surrendered.

sentences.zh: 詐都亦降于蒲家奴，於是撫甯諸路如舊時。

translations.literal: Zhadou also surrendered to Pujianu; thereupon all routes were pacified as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhadou yielded to Pujianu, and the frontier was quiet again.

sentences.zh: 太師因致穆宗，教統門、渾蠢、耶悔、星顯四路及嶺東諸部自今勿復稱都部長。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor therefore sent word to Muzong, instructing the four routes of Tongmen, Hunchun, Yehui, and Xingxian and the eastern-ridge tribes that from now on they must not again style themselves dubuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor wrote Muzong: the Tongmen, Hunchun, Yehui, and Xingxian routes and the eastern-ridge tribes were never again to call themselves dubuzhang (tribal chiefs).

sentences.zh: 命勝官、醜阿等撫定乙離骨嶺注阿門水之西諸部居民，又命斡帶及偏裨悉平二涅囊虎、二蠢出等路寇盜而還。

translations.literal: He ordered Shengguan, Chou’a, and the rest to pacify the residents west of Yiligu ridge at Zhu’amen River, and also ordered Wodai and the flank officers to pacify bandits on the Ernie’nanghu and Erchun routes and return.
translations.idiomatic: Shengguan, Chou’a, and others were sent to settle the peoples west of Yiligu ridge on the Zhu’amen River; Wodai and his captains cleared the Ernie’nanghu and Erchun roads of raiders and came home.

sentences.zh: 七年庚辰，劾者尚守阿疏城，毛睹祿來降。

translations.literal: In year seven, gengchen, Hezhe still held Ashu city; Maoduilu came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, gengchen (1100), Hezhe still held Ashu; Maoduilu submitted.

sentences.zh: 阿疏猶在遼，遼使使來罷兵。

translations.literal: Ashu was still in the Liao; the Liao sent an envoy to order a ceasefire.
translations.idiomatic: Ashu remained at the Liao court, and the Liao sent to halt the fighting.

sentences.zh: 未到，穆宗使烏林答石魯往佐劾者，戒之曰：「遼使來罷兵，但換我軍衣服旗幟與阿疏城中無辨，勿令遼使知之。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Muzong sent Wulin Da Shilu to aid Hezhe and warned him: “When the Liao envoy comes to cease hostilities, only change our army’s clothes and banners so they cannot be told from Ashu city—do not let the Liao envoy know.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy came, Muzong sent Wulin Da Shilu to help Hezhe with orders: “When the Liao man comes to stop the war, swap our men’s dress and flags for the garrison’s so he cannot tell us apart.

sentences.zh: 」因戒劾者曰：「遼使可以計卻，勿聽其言遽罷兵也。

translations.literal: ” He also warned Hezhe: “The Liao envoy can be driven off by stratagem; do not heed his words and hastily cease hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: ” He told Hezhe too, “You can trick the envoy away—do not obey him and lay down arms at once.

sentences.zh: 」遼使果來罷兵，穆宗使蒲察部胡魯勃堇、邈遜孛堇與俱至阿疏城。

translations.literal: ” The Liao envoy indeed came to cease hostilities; Muzong sent Pucha division’s Hulubojin and Miaosun Beijin to go with him to Ashu city.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Liao envoy came as expected. Muzong sent Hulubojin of the Pucha and Miaosun Beijin with him to Ashu.

sentences.zh: 劾者見遼使，詭謂胡魯、邈遜曰：「我部族自相攻擊，幹汝等何事？

translations.literal: Hezhe, seeing the Liao envoy, deceived Hulu and Miaosun, saying: “Our tribes attack one another—what business is it of yours?
translations.idiomatic: Hezhe met the envoy and lied to Hulu and Miaosun: “We are fighting our own kin—what is that to you?

sentences.zh: 誰識汝之太師？

translations.literal: Who knows your Grand Preceptor?
translations.idiomatic: Who ever heard of your Grand Preceptor?

sentences.zh: 」乃援創刺殺胡魯、邈遜所乘馬。

translations.literal: ” He then drew his sword and stabbed the horses Hulu and Miaosun rode.
translations.idiomatic: ” He drew his sword and lunged at their horses.

sentences.zh: 遼使驚駭遽走，不敢回顧，徑歸。

translations.literal: The Liao envoy, startled and terrified, fled at once, dared not look back, and went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy bolted in terror without a backward glance and rode straight for the border.

sentences.zh: 居數日，破其城。

translations.literal: After several days they stormed the city.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the town was taken by storm.

sentences.zh: 狄故保還自遼。

translations.literal: Digubao returned from the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Digubao came back from the Liao.

sentences.zh: 在城中，執而殺之。

translations.literal: He was in the city; they seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He was inside; they seized him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 阿疏復訴於遼。

translations.literal: Ashu again appealed to the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Ashu appealed to the Liao once more.

sentences.zh: 遼遣奚節度使乙烈來。

translations.literal: The Liao sent Xi military commissioner Yilie.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao dispatched Xi frontier commissioner Yilie.

sentences.zh: 穆宗至來流水興和村，見乙烈。

translations.literal: Muzong went to Laishui Xinghe village and met Yilie.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong went to Xinghe on the Laishui and received Yilie.

sentences.zh: 問阿疏城事，命穆宗曰：「凡攻城所獲，存者復與之，不存者備償。

translations.literal: Asked about the Ashu city affair, he ordered Muzong: “Whatever is taken in storming a city—if alive, return them; if dead, provide compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Yilie asked about Ashu and commanded Muzong: “For everything seized in a siege, return the living; for the dead, pay indemnity.

sentences.zh: 」且征馬數百匹。

translations.literal: ” and moreover levied several hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: ” and demanded several hundred horses besides.

sentences.zh: 穆宗與僚佐謀曰：「若償阿疏，則諸部不復可號令任使也。

translations.literal: Muzong consulted his staff, saying: “If we compensate Ashu, the tribes will no longer heed command or assignment.”
translations.idiomatic: Muzong told his counselors, “Pay Ashu off, and no tribe will take orders from us again.”

sentences.zh: 」乃令主隈、禿答兩水之民陽爲阻絕鷹路，復使鱉故德部節度使言于遼曰：「欲開鷹路，非生女直節度使不可。

translations.literal: ” He then had the people of the Zhuwei and Tuda two rivers feign blocking the hawk road, and again had the military commissioner of the Bie Gude tribe speak to Liao, saying: “To open the hawk road, nothing short of the Sheng Jurchen military commissioner will do.”
translations.idiomatic: ” He staged a blockade of the hawk road by Zhuwei and Tuda tribesmen and had the Bie Gude commissioner tell the Liao, “Only the commissioner of the uncooked Jurchen can reopen the hawk road.”

sentences.zh: 」遼不知其爲穆宗謀也，信之，命穆宗討阻絕鷹路者，而阿疏城事遂止。

translations.literal: ” Liao, unaware this was Muzong’s stratagem, believed it, ordered Muzong to punish those who blocked the hawk road, and the matter of Ashu city thereupon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Liao court, duped, told Muzong to crush the blockaders—and the Ashu affair died away.

sentences.zh: 穆宗聲言平鷹路，畋于土溫水而歸。

translations.literal: Muzong announced he had pacified the hawk road, hunted on the Tuwen River, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong proclaimed the hawk road secure, hunted along the Tuwen River, and came home.

sentences.zh: 是歲，留可來降。

translations.literal: In that year Liuke came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liuke submitted.

sentences.zh: 八年辛巳，遼使使持賜物來賞平鷹路之有功者。

translations.literal: In year eight, xinsi, Liao sent envoys bearing gifts to reward those who had merit in pacifying the hawk road.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1101) envoys from Liao arrived with gifts for those who had “pacified” the hawk road.

sentences.zh: 九年壬午，使蒲家奴以遼賜，給主隈、禿答之民，且修鷹路而歸。

translations.literal: In year nine, renwu, he sent Pujianu with Liao’s gifts to give to the Zhuwei and Tuda people, and also repaired the hawk road before returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1102) he sent Pujianu to pay Zhuwei and Tuda with Liao gifts, reopened the hawk road, and came back.

sentences.zh: 冬，蕭海里叛，入於系案女直阿典部，遣其族人斡達剌來給結和，曰：「願與太師爲友，同往伐遼。

translations.literal: In winter Xiao Haili rebelled, entered the Adian tribe of the Xi’an Jurchen, and sent his clansman Wodala to propose alliance, saying: “I wish to be friends with the Grand Master and together go attack Liao.”
translations.idiomatic: That winter Xiao Haili rebelled and took refuge with the Adian Jurchen. His kinsman Wodala came offering alliance: “Let us be allies, Grand Master, and march on the Liao together.”

sentences.zh: 」穆宗執斡達剌。

translations.literal: ” Muzong seized Wodala.
translations.idiomatic: ” Muzong took Wodala prisoner.

sentences.zh: 會遼命穆宗捕討海里，穆宗送斡達剌於遼，募軍得甲千餘。

translations.literal: It happened that Liao ordered Muzong to hunt down Haili; Muzong sent Wodala to Liao and levied troops, obtaining more than a thousand armored men.
translations.idiomatic: Liao then ordered Muzong to pursue Haili. He handed Wodala over and mustered troops—over a thousand men in armor.

sentences.zh: 女直甲兵之數，始見於此，蓋未嘗滿千也。

translations.literal: The number of Jurchen armored soldiers is first seen here; they had never before reached a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first record of Jurchen armored strength at such a scale—they had never mustered a full thousand before.

sentences.zh: 軍次混同水，蕭海里再使人來，復執之。

translations.literal: The army halted at the Huntong River; Xiao Haili sent envoys again, and they were seized again.
translations.idiomatic: The host camped on the Huntong. Haili sent another embassy; again Muzong took them prisoner.

sentences.zh: 既而與海里遇。

translations.literal: Presently they met Haili.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the armies met.

sentences.zh: 海里遙問曰：「我使者安在？

translations.literal: Haili called from afar: “Where are my envoys?”
translations.idiomatic: Haili shouted across the field, “Where are my messengers?”

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「與後人偕來。

translations.literal: ” The answer came: “They came along with those in the rear.”
translations.idiomatic: ” “They are coming with the rear guard,” came the reply.

sentences.zh: 」海里不信。

translations.literal: ” Haili did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: ” He did not believe them.

sentences.zh: 是時，遼追海里兵數千人，攻之不能克。

translations.literal: At this time Liao pursuit troops, several thousand, attacked him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of Liao pursuers had already failed to break him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗謂遼將曰：「退爾軍，我當獨取海里。

translations.literal: Muzong said to the Liao general: “Withdraw your army; I alone shall take Haili.”
translations.idiomatic: Muzong told the Liao commander, “Pull your men back—I will take Haili myself.”

sentences.zh: 」遼將許之。

translations.literal: ” The Liao general assented.
translations.idiomatic: ” The commander agreed.

sentences.zh: 太祖策馬突戰，流矢中海里首，海里墮馬下，執而殺之，大破其軍。

translations.literal: Taizu spurred his horse and charged; a stray arrow struck Haili’s head; Haili fell from his horse, was seized and killed, and his army was utterly broken.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu (Grand Ancestor) charged. A stray arrow struck Haili in the head; he fell from his horse, was seized and slain, and his host was shattered.

sentences.zh: 使阿離合懣獻馘於遼。

translations.literal: He sent Alihemen to present the severed heads to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Alihemen was sent to offer the trophies to the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 金人自此知遼兵之易與也。

translations.literal: From this the Jin people knew how easy Liao troops were to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the Jurchen knew the Liao soldier was no match for them.

sentences.zh: 是役也，康宗最先登，於是以先登並有功者爲前行，次以諸軍護俘獲歸所部。

translations.literal: In this campaign Kangzong was first to mount; therefore those who first mounted and had merit formed the vanguard, next all armies escorted captives back to their commands.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong was first over the wall. Men who led the assault marched in the van; the rest guarded prisoners home to their camps.

sentences.zh: 穆宗朝遼主於漁所，大被嘉賞，授以使相，錫予加等。

translations.literal: Muzong attended the Liao ruler at the fishing grounds, was greatly praised and rewarded, granted envoy-and-chancellor rank, with gifts raised a grade.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong attended the Liao emperor at the autumn fishing hunt and came away laden with praise, the rank of envoy-chancellor, and lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 十年癸未二月，穆宗還。

translations.literal: In year ten, guimao, second month, Muzong returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1104), second month, Muzong came home.

sentences.zh: 遼使使授從破海里者官賞。

translations.literal: Liao sent envoys to bestow offices and rewards on those who had joined in defeating Haili.
translations.idiomatic: Liao envoys arrived to reward every man who had fought at Haili.

sentences.zh: 高麗始來通好。

translations.literal: Goryeo for the first time came to open friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo opened diplomatic ties for the first time.

sentences.zh: 十月二十九日，穆宗卒，年五十有一。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month Muzong died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth of the tenth month Muzong died, aged fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 初，諸部各有信牌，穆宗用太祖議，擅置牌號者置於法，自是號令乃一，民聽不疑矣。

translations.literal: At first each tribe had its own tally-tokens; Muzong, following Taizu’s counsel, put those who set up tokens on their own under the law; from then commands were one, and the people heard without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Each tribe had once carried its own tokens. At Taizu’s urging Muzong outlawed private tally-marks; from then on one law spoke, and the people obeyed without question.

sentences.zh: 自景祖以來，兩世四主，志業相因，卒定離析，一切治以本部法令，東南至於乙離骨、曷懶、耶懶、土骨論，東北至於五國、主隈、禿答，金蓋盛於此。

translations.literal: From Jingzu on, two generations and four lords, ambition and achievement continuing one from another, at last settled fragmentation; all was governed by this tribe’s laws—southeast to Yiligu, Halian, Yelang, and Tugulun, northeast to the Five States, Zhuwei, and Tuda; the Jin house flourished to this extent.
translations.idiomatic: From Jingzu through four rulers in two generations, one policy built on the last until the tribes were one. Tribal law ruled from Yiligu, Halian, Yelang, and Tugulun in the southeast to the Five States, Zhuwei, and Tuda in the northeast—the Jurchen power stood at its height.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，追諡孝平皇帝，廟號穆宗。

translations.literal: In Tianhui year fifteen posthumously titled Emperor Xiaoping, temple name Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year fifteen (1137) he was posthumously named Emperor Xiaoping, temple name Muzong.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏曰獻陵。

translations.literal: In Huangtong year four his tomb was styled Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year four (1144) his tomb was named Xianling.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡章順孝平皇帝。

translations.literal: In year five, additional title: Manifest and compliant, filial and peaceful emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his title was raised to Manifest Grace Filial Peace Emperor.

sentences.zh: 兄子康宗，諱烏雅束，字毛路完，世祖長子也。

translations.literal: Nephew Kangzong, taboo name Wuyashu, style Maoluwan, eldest son of Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Kangzong (Sagacious Ancestor), personal name Wuyashu, courtesy name Maoluwan, was Shizu’s eldest son.

sentences.zh: 遼清甯七年辛丑歲生。

translations.literal: Born in Liao Qingning year seven, year xinchou.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in Liao Qingning year seven (1061).

sentences.zh: 乾統三年癸未，襲節度使，年四十三。

translations.literal: In Qiantong year three, guiwei, he succeeded to military commissioner, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiantong year three (1103) he inherited the commissionership, aged forty-three.

sentences.zh: 穆宗末年，阿疏使達紀誘扇邊民，曷懶甸人執送之。

translations.literal: In Muzong’s late years Ashu’s envoy Daji enticed and incited border people; Halian district people seized and sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Muzong’s reign Ashu’s agent Daji stirred up the frontier tribes; Halian men seized him and delivered him up.

sentences.zh: 穆宗使石適歡撫納曷懶甸，未行，穆宗卒，至是遣焉。

translations.literal: Muzong had sent Shishihuan to pacify and accept Halian district; he had not yet gone when Muzong died; at this time he was dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong had named Shishihuan to pacify Halian, but Muzong died before he marched; now Kangzong sent him.

sentences.zh: 先是，高麗通好，既而頗有隙，高麗使來請議事，使者至高麗，拒而不納。

translations.literal: Earlier Goryeo had opened relations; afterward there was considerable rift; Goryeo sent envoys to request deliberation; when the messenger reached Goryeo, they refused and would not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Diplomacy with Goryeo had soured. Goryeo asked to parley; when the Jurchen envoy reached the Goryeo court, he was turned away.

sentences.zh: 五水之民附於高麗，執團練使十四人。

translations.literal: The people of the Five Waters attached themselves to Goryeo and seized fourteen regimental-training commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Five Waters tribes went over to Goryeo and took fourteen regimental commissioners prisoner.

sentences.zh: 語在《高麗傳》中。

translations.literal: The account is in the “Annals of Goryeo.”
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in the Goryeo monograph.

sentences.zh: 二年甲申，高麗再來伐，石適歡再破之。

translations.literal: In year two, jiashen, Goryeo again came to attack; Shishihuan again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1104) Goryeo invaded again; Shishihuan beat them back again.

sentences.zh: 高麗復請和，前所執團練十四人皆遣歸，石適歡撫定邊民而還。

translations.literal: Goryeo again sued for peace; the fourteen regimental-training commissioners previously seized were all sent back; Shishihuan pacified and settled the border people and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sued for peace, returned the fourteen captives, and Shishihuan quieted the frontier before coming home.

sentences.zh: 蘇濱水民不聽命，使斡帶至活羅海川，召諸官僚告諭之。

translations.literal: The Subin River people would not heed commands; he sent Wandai to the Huoluo Sea River to summon the various officials and admonish them.
translations.idiomatic: Subin River tribes defied orders. Wandai was sent to the Huoluo Sea to summon their chiefs and read them the law.

sentences.zh: 含國部蘇濱水居斡豁勃堇不至。

translations.literal: Wohe Bojian of the Subin River dwelling in the Hanguo tribe did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Wohe, the Bojian of Subin in Hanguo, stayed away.

sentences.zh: 斡准部、職德部既至，復亡去。

translations.literal: The Wozhun tribe and the Zhide tribe, having come, again fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs of Wozhun and Zhide appeared, then slipped away again.

sentences.zh: 塢塔遇二部于馬紀嶺，執之而來，遂伐斡豁，克之。

translations.literal: Wuta encountered the two tribes at Maji Ridge, seized them and came; thereupon he attacked Wohe and overcame him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuta intercepted the defectors at Maji Ridge, took them prisoner, then marched on Wohe and overthrew him.

sentences.zh: 斡帶進至北琴海，攻拔泓忒城，乃還。

translations.literal: Wandai advanced to the North Qin Sea, attacked and took Hongte city, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wandai pushed to the North Qin Sea, stormed Hongte fort, and turned home.

sentences.zh: 四年丙戌，高麗遣黑歡方石來賀襲位，遣杯魯報之。

translations.literal: In year four, bingxu, Goryeo sent Heihuan Fangshi to congratulate the succession; [Kangzong] sent Beilu to return the compliment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1106) Goryeo sent Heihuan Fangshi to hail the new rule; Kangzong sent Beilu in return.

sentences.zh: 高麗約還諸亡在彼者，乃使阿聒、勝昆往受之。

translations.literal: Goryeo agreed to return all fugitives who had fled there, and so Asuo and Shengkun were sent to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo promised to return everyone who had taken refuge in its territory, and Asuo and Shengkun were dispatched to take charge of the handover.

sentences.zh: 高麗背約，殺二使，築九城於曷懶甸，以兵數萬來攻。

translations.literal: Goryeo broke the agreement, killed the two envoys, built nine fortresses in Yilan Circuit, and came to attack with tens of thousands of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo broke faith, executed both envoys, erected nine walled posts in Yilan Circuit, and attacked with an army numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 斡賽敗之。

translations.literal: Wosai defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wosai defeated the Goryeo forces.

sentences.zh: 斡魯亦築九城，與高麗九城相對。

translations.literal: Wulu also built nine fortresses, facing the nine Goryeo fortresses across from them.
translations.idiomatic: Wulu likewise built nine fortresses, set directly opposite Goryeo’s nine posts.

sentences.zh: 高麗復來攻，斡賽復敗之。

translations.literal: Goryeo attacked again, and Wosai defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo attacked once more, Wosai routed them again.

sentences.zh: 高麗約以還逋逃之人，退九城之軍。

translations.literal: Goryeo agreed to return the fugitives and withdraw the army from the nine fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo agreed to surrender the fugitives and pull its troops back from the nine fortresses.

sentences.zh: 復所侵故地。

translations.literal: They also restored the territory that had been seized.
translations.idiomatic: They also returned the lands they had invaded.

sentences.zh: 九月，乃罷兵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, hostilities were halted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the armies stood down.

sentences.zh: 七年己丑，歲不登，減盜賊征償，振貧乏者。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, jichou, the harvest failed; indemnities for theft were reduced, and the poor were relieved.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (jichou) crops failed; the court lowered theft penalties and provided relief to the destitute.

sentences.zh: 十一年癸巳，康宗卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, guisi, Kangzong died at the age of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (guisi) Kangzong died, aged fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，追諡恭簡皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he received the posthumous title Emperor Gongjian.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏曰喬陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong, his burial mound was named Qiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong his tomb precinct was named Qiaoling.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡康宗獻敏恭簡皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, his posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Xianmin Gongjian of Kangzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was expanded to Emperor Xianmin Gongjian of Kangzong.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金之厥初，兄弟三人，亦微矣。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: At the very beginning of Jin, the three brothers were indeed insignificant.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser writes: In Jin’s earliest days the three brothers were humble indeed.

sentences.zh: 熙宗追帝祖宗，定著始祖、景祖、世祖廟，世世不祧。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong traced the imperial clan’s forebears and fixed the temples of the Founding Ancestor, Jingzu, and Shizu, which were never to be removed from the ancestral roster.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong traced the lineage of the imperial house and established the shrines of the Founding Ancestor, Jingzu, and Shizu, never to be displaced from the main line of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 始祖娶六十之婦而生二男一女，豈非天耶？

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor took a wife of sixty years and fathered two sons and one daughter—was this not Heaven’s doing?
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor married a woman of sixty and fathered two sons and a daughter—could that have been anything but Heaven’s design?

sentences.zh: 景祖不受遼籍遼印，取雅達國相以與其子。

translations.literal: Jingzu refused Liao registration and Liao seals, and took the Liao state chancellor Yada and gave him to his son.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu refused to be registered by Liao or to accept Liao seals, took the Liao state chancellor Yada, and assigned him to his son.

sentences.zh: 世祖既破桓赧、散達，遼政日衰，而以太祖屬之穆宗，其思慮豈不深遠矣夫！

translations.literal: After Shizu had defeated Huanzan and Sandá, Liao government daily declined; yet he entrusted Taizu to Muzong—how far-reaching his deliberation was!
translations.idiomatic: Once Shizu had broken Huanzan and Sandá and Liao power was waning day by day, he nevertheless placed Taizu under Muzong’s care—what long-range foresight that showed!
